name: Deuteronomy
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel on the east side of the Jordan, out in the desert, in the Arabah{a} opposite Suph,{b} somewhere between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di Zahab.{c}
(Going from Horeb{d} to Kadesh Barnea along the Mount Seir road normally takes eleven days.)
It was the first day of the eleventh month (January-February),{e} forty years after leaving Egypt, when Moses gave the Israelites a full report of all that Yahweh{f} had told him to pass on to them.
By then he had beaten Sihon, the Amorite king whose capital was Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan, whose home was in Ashtaroth and{g} Edrei.
There in Moab’s country, east of the Jordan, Moses set about spelling out this teaching.{h} His words were:
“While we were at Horeb, Yahweh our God told us, ‘Your stay at this mountain has gone on long enough.

Pack up and go. March to the Amorites’ hills and to every region next to them: the Arabah, the highlands, the Shephelah,{i} the Negev,{j} the seacoast, Canaanite country, and Lebanon, on to the great river Euphrates.
Here it is. I am putting the land before you. Enter it and claim what Yahweh swore{k} to hand over to your forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to the generations after them.’
“I said to you then, ‘Carrying you is more than I can do alone.
Yahweh your God has multiplied you. Look at you today, as many as the stars overhead.
I pray that Yahweh, your ancestors’ God, will multiply you a thousandfold and bless you the way he said he would!
Yet how could I bear alone the whole weight of you, your troubles, and your disputes?
From every tribe, pick men known for wisdom and good sense, and I will make them your leaders.’
Your reply was, ‘We like what you suggest.’
So I took tribal leaders, men who were wise and respected, and put them in authority over you, each in charge of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, or ten, with other officials for the tribes.
My instructions to your judges then were: ‘Hear the quarrels between your fellow Israelites{l} and rule justly, whether it involves two Israelites or an Israelite and the outsider staying with him.
No favorites in court. The lowly and the great get the same hearing. Fear nobody, because the verdict is God’s. When a matter is beyond you, send it up to me and I will listen.’
That was also when I gave you orders about all the rest of your duties.
“Next we left Horeb and walked the whole of that vast, dreadful desert you remember, toward the Amorite hills, as Yahweh our God had ordered, until we reached Kadesh Barnea.
I said to you, ‘This is the Amorites’ hill country, and Yahweh our God is giving it to us.
Yahweh your God has laid the country out before you. Climb up and claim it, as he, the God of your ancestors, said you should. Have no fear, and do not lose courage.’
“Then every one of you came up and said, ‘First let us send scouts ahead. They can examine the land and report on the road we should take and the towns we will meet.’
This seemed sensible to me, and I chose twelve men, one for each tribe.
They left, climbed into the hills, arrived at the Valley of Eshcol,{m} and looked it over.
Taking some of the produce of that country in their hands, they carried it back down to us and announced, ‘Yahweh our God is giving us a fine land.’
“But you would not climb. Yahweh your God gave an order, and you rebelled.
In your tents you muttered, ‘Yahweh hates us. He took us out of Egypt only to give us to the Amorites to be wiped out.

Where are we going? Our own brothers have taken the courage out of us by reporting that these people are stronger and taller than we are, with cities as big as fortresses and walls rising to the clouds. They also spotted Anakim{n} there.’
“I answered, ‘Don’t panic, and don’t be afraid of them.
Yahweh your God walks ahead of you. He will do the fighting for you, as he did before your eyes in Egypt,
and in the wilderness. There you saw how Yahweh your God held you up as a father holds up his child, all along your road until you got here.’
Even so, you put no trust in Yahweh your God,
who led the way ahead of you, scouting out your campsites, by fire at night to show you the path, and by cloud in daylight.
“When Yahweh heard your words, his anger rose, and he made this vow:
‘Not one man of this wicked generation will see the fine land I vowed to hand over to your ancestors.
Caleb{o} son of Jephunneh alone will see it. I will hand him and his children the ground he has walked across, since he followed Yahweh wholeheartedly.’
Because of you, Yahweh was angry with me as well. ‘Not even you will go in,’ he said.
‘Joshua{p} son of Nun, who serves you, will be the one. Build him up, since he will bring Israel into possession of it.
And those little ones you called prey, and the children who still cannot tell good from bad, will enter. The land will be theirs, and they will own it.
But you must turn back and go into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea.’{r}
“You replied, ‘We have sinned against Yahweh. Now we will go up and fight, as Yahweh our God ordered us.’ Each man buckled on his weapons, treating the climb into the hills as nothing.
Yahweh then said to me, ‘Give them this warning: Stay below, no fighting. I will not be in your ranks, so your enemies will crush you.’
So I warned you, and you paid no attention. You rebelled against Yahweh’s order and, full of pride, climbed the hills anyway.
Out came the Amorites who lived in those hills. Like a swarm of bees they chased you and cut you down all the way from Seir{s} to Hormah.
Back you came, sobbing before Yahweh, but he turned a deaf ear and gave you no notice.
That is why you spent so many days at Kadesh, the days you spent there.”

notes.text: The Arabah is the great rift valley running south from the Sea of Galilee through the Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba.
Hebrew Suph, “reeds,” perhaps short for Yam Suph, the Sea of Reeds. The Greek Old Testament has “near the Red Sea.” The places named in this verse cannot be located with certainty.
Di Zahab means “plenty of gold.” Paran perhaps means “place of caves,” Laban “white,” and Hazeroth “enclosures” or “villages.”
Horeb, perhaps “dry” or “wasteland,” is the name Deuteronomy usually gives the mountain called Sinai in Exodus. Kadesh means “holy.”

Hebrew “the eleventh month,” later called Shevat. This translation counts months from the spring new year (Nisan, also called Abib, in March-April). The Hebrew calendar follows the moon, so modern dates are approximate.
Yahweh is the personal name of Israel’s God (Hebrew YHWH), which many English Bibles replace with “the LORD.” See Exodus 3:14-15. Moses means “drawn out” (Exodus 2:10).
So the Greek Old Testament (compare Joshua 12:4). The Hebrew has no “and.” Sihon’s name may mean “sweeping away,” Heshbon “reckoning,” and Ashtaroth is named for the goddess Astarte.
Or “law.” Hebrew torah means instruction or teaching, and in Deuteronomy it often means the whole body of teaching Moses gives.
The Shephelah, “lowland,” is the band of low hills between the central highlands and the coastal plain.
The Negev, “dry land,” is the dry south of the country.
Hebrew “that Yahweh swore.” The Greek Old Testament reads “that I swore.”
Hebrew “your brothers,” used often in Deuteronomy for fellow Israelites.
Eshcol means “cluster,” as of grapes. See Numbers 13:23-24.
The Anakim were a people remembered for their great size. Anak may mean “long-necked.” The Greek Old Testament has “the sons of the giants.”
Caleb probably means “dog,” perhaps in the sense of a faithful servant.
Joshua means “Yahweh saves.”
Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here probably the Gulf of Aqaba.
So the Greek Old Testament and other ancient versions. The Hebrew reads “in Seir.” Hormah means “destruction.”

subheads.19: The people refuse to enter the land

verses.text: “Then we swung around and set out into the desert on the road to the Red Sea,{a} as Yahweh had directed me, and for a long time we went around Mount Seir.
Then Yahweh said to me,
‘You have gone around this highland long enough. Now head north.
Tell the people this: You will soon be passing through land that belongs to your cousins, Esau’s descendants,{b} who live in Seir. They fear you, so take great care.
Do not provoke them. Not even a footprint of their ground will be yours, since I handed the Seir highlands to Esau for his own.
Pay for your food with silver. Pay silver for your drinking water too.
Yahweh your God has blessed all your work. He has kept track of your walk through this vast desert. These forty years he has stayed with you, and you have never lacked a thing.’
“So we moved past our cousins, Esau’s descendants in Seir, leaving the Arabah road and Elath and Ezion Geber{c} behind, and took the road toward the Desert of Moab.
Yahweh warned me, ‘Leave Moab alone, and do not go to war against them. None of their land will become yours, because Ar{d} is what I assigned to the descendants of Lot.{e}’
(Long ago the Emim{f} lived there, a mighty, large people, tall like the Anakim.
People grouped them with the Rephaim,{g} as they did the Anakim, but Moabites say Emim.
In Seir, the Horites{h} had lived before Esau’s descendants pushed them out, destroyed them, and took the land. That is just what Israel would do in the country Yahweh was giving them.)
‘Up now, and over the Zered Valley.’{i} We went across.
Between leaving Kadesh Barnea and crossing the Zered, thirty-eight years went by. In that time the whole generation of fighting men died off in the camp, as Yahweh had promised.
Yahweh’s own hand worked against them, clearing them out of the camp until none remained.
“After the last of the warriors was dead and gone,
Yahweh spoke to me and said,
‘Today is the day you cross Moab’s border at Ar.
Once you are near the Ammonites, do not pester them or draw them into a fight. No part of their country will go to you, because I gave it to Lot’s descendants.’
(This also was thought of as giants’ country. Giants had lived there once, but Ammonites knew them as Zamzummim.{j}
These were a mighty, numerous people, tall like the Anakim. Yahweh destroyed them for the Ammonites, who evicted them and moved in.
So he had done for Esau’s descendants in Seir, whom he helped by destroying the Horites. They took their place, and live there still.
In the same way, the Avvim,{k} who lived in villages out to Gaza, were destroyed by newcomers from Caphtor,{l} who settled in their territory.)
‘Up, and march! Cross the gorge of the Arnon.{m} I am handing you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, with his country. Begin taking it, and give him battle.
Beginning today, I will fill the nations all over the earth with dread of you. Hearing of you, they will shake and be sick with fear.’
“From the Kedemoth{n} desert I sent men to Sihon king of Heshbon with an offer of peace:
‘Allow us to cross your territory. We will keep strictly to the road and will not stray to either side.
Sell us food, and we will pay in silver. Give us water, and we will pay in silver. All we ask is to pass through on foot,
as Esau’s people in Seir and the Moabites in Ar allowed me, until I cross the Jordan to the country Yahweh our God is giving us.’
Sihon, king of Heshbon, did not agree to our passing. Yahweh your God had hardened his spirit and stiffened his heart, to deliver him to you, as you see today.
Yahweh told me, ‘I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land to you. Take it, so you may own his land.’
Sihon marched out with all his troops to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
Yahweh our God turned him over to us, and we struck down him, his sons,{o} and his entire force.
In that campaign we seized every one of his cities and placed each under the ban,{p} destroying men, women, and children alike. Nobody was left alive.
We took as loot only the animals and whatever we found in the cities we captured.
Starting at Aroer on the Arnon gorge’s rim, and the city within the gorge itself, through to Gilead, no city stood too high for us. Yahweh our God gave every one to us.
You alone kept clear of the Ammonites’ country, the full length of the Jabbok River bank,{q} the hill cities, and whatever other place Yahweh our God had banned.”

notes.text: Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here probably the Gulf of Aqaba. See the note at 1:40.
Esau means “hairy” (Genesis 25:25). Seir also suggests “hairy,” perhaps for its wooded slopes.
Elath, “terebinth,” and Ezion Geber were at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.
Ar, “city,” was a city or district of Moab.
Lot may mean “covering.” Moab and Ammon came from him (Genesis 19:36-38).
Emim means “terrors.”
The Rephaim were an ancient people remembered as giants. The same word elsewhere means the spirits of the dead.
The Horites may be “cave dwellers,” or the name may point to the Hurrians.
Hebrew nahal, a valley with a stream that flows mainly in the rainy season. Zered may mean “willow.”
Zamzummim may mean “murmurers.” The meaning is uncertain.
Avvim may mean “ruins.”
Caphtor is usually identified with Crete. The Philistines came from there (Amos 9:7).
The Arnon is the gorge east of the Dead Sea that formed Moab’s northern border. Its name may mean “roaring stream.”
Kedemoth means “eastern places.” Jahaz (verse 32) may mean “trampled place.”
So the Hebrew reading tradition. The written text has “his son.”
Hebrew herem: giving something over completely to God, which in war meant destroying it entirely.
The Jabbok, perhaps “flowing,” is a stream that runs west into the Jordan.

verses.text: “Next we headed north on the Bashan road. Og, the king of Bashan, brought out his whole army and met us in battle at Edrei.
Yahweh said to me, ‘Fear him not. Og, his people, and his land are already in your power. Do to him what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king whose throne was at Heshbon.’
And so Yahweh our God put Og and all his troops in our power as well. We fought until he had no survivors.
We captured every one of his cities that day. Of sixty towns in the whole Argob{a} region, Og’s realm in Bashan, there was not one we failed to take.
Each of these was a walled city with high ramparts, gates, and bolts. Many unwalled villages came with them.
As with Sihon of Heshbon, we put each of these cities under the ban, wiping out men, women, and children.
The livestock and everything valuable in the cities, however, we kept for ourselves.
“By then we had seized from the two Amorite kings their whole territory east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge up to Mount Hermon.{b}
(Sidonians say Sirion for Hermon, while Amorites say Senir.)
We held every city of the tableland, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan out to Salecah and Edrei, cities that had belonged to Og’s kingdom.

(Og of Bashan was the sole one left from the Rephaim. His bed{c} was iron, and it is still on display in the Ammonite city of Rabbah. By an ordinary forearm’s measure it is nine cubits by four,{d} roughly thirteen and a half feet by six.)
“Here is how I divided the land we took then. Reuben and Gad received the area from Aroer, on the Arnon Gorge’s edge, and half the hill country of Gilead, towns included.
The rest of Gilead, and all of Bashan, Og’s former realm, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (The whole Argob district of Bashan used to be called Rephaim country.
Jair,{e} a man of Manasseh, took the entire Argob region as far as the borders of Geshur and Maacah. He gave Bashan his own name, Havvoth Jair,{f} which remains today.)
Gilead went to Machir.{g}
To Reuben and Gad I gave the land running from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the gorge as a boundary, and on to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
It included the Arabah, bounded by the Jordan, from Chinnereth{h} south to the Sea of the Arabah, which is the Dead Sea,{i} at the foot of Pisgah’s{j} eastern slopes.
“I gave you these orders then: ‘Yahweh your God has handed you this land as your own. Every one of you able to fight must cross ahead of your fellow Israelites, fully armed.
Your wives, your children, and your herds (which I know are many) may stay in the towns I have given you.

This lasts until Yahweh lets your relatives rest, as he has you, and they own the country Yahweh your God is about to give them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return home to what I gave you.’
“To Joshua I said at that time, ‘Your eyes saw everything Yahweh your God did to these two kings. Every kingdom you are about to enter will get the same from him.
Do not be afraid of them. Yahweh your God himself will fight for you.’
“I also pleaded with Yahweh then:
‘Lord Yahweh,{k} you have started to show me, your servant, how great you are and how strong your hand is. What god in heaven or on earth can do what you do or match your power?
Please let me go across and look at the rich country beyond the Jordan, the lovely hills and Lebanon.’
Because of you, Yahweh was furious with me, and he refused me. ‘That is enough,’ he said. ‘Never raise this with me again.
Climb to the summit of Pisgah. Gaze west, north, south, and east, and take in the view yourself. You will not be crossing this Jordan.
Commission Joshua. Cheer him on and make him strong, since he will lead these people across and divide among them the land you will see.’
We remained, then, in the valley opposite Beth Peor.{l}”

notes.text: Argob may mean “heap of stones.”
Hermon means “sacred” or “devoted.” Sirion and Senir may both mean “breastplate,” perhaps from the shine of snow on the mountain.
Or “coffin” or “sarcophagus”; the Hebrew word usually means a bed or couch.
Hebrew “nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by a man’s cubit.” A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters).
Jair means “he gives light.”
Havvoth Jair means “tent villages of Jair.”
Machir means “sold.” He was a son of Manasseh (Genesis 50:23). Manasseh means “causing to forget” (Genesis 41:51).
Chinnereth, perhaps “harp-shaped,” is the Sea of Galilee.
Hebrew “Salt Sea.”
Pisgah is a ridge of the Abarim mountains northeast of the Dead Sea, near Mount Nebo.
Hebrew Adonai Yahweh.
Beth Peor means “house of Peor,” a place linked with worship of the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25).

subheads.23: Moses Is Not Allowed to Enter

verses.text: “Now, Israel, pay attention to the laws and rulings I am teaching you to follow. Obey them and you will live, and you will go in and own the land Yahweh, your ancestors’ God, is giving you.
Add nothing to what I am telling you, and take nothing away. Just keep every command of Yahweh your God that I am passing on to you.
With your own eyes you watched what Yahweh did at Baal Peor.{a} Anyone among you who followed the Baal of Peor was wiped out by Yahweh your God.
You who stayed loyal to Yahweh your God, though, are all living this very day.
Notice that I have handed you laws and rulings just as Yahweh my God commanded me. You are to live by them once you enter the country you are going to own.

Hold to them and put them into practice. That will prove to other nations that you have wisdom and insight. They will hear all these laws and remark, ‘What a wise, insightful people, this great nation!’
Is there any great nation whose god stays as near as Yahweh our God stays near to us whenever we call?
Is there any great nation with rules and rulings as just as this whole teaching that I put before you today?
“Only be careful. Guard your own lives, so you never forget what your eyes have seen, and so it never fades from your memory as long as you live. Pass it on to your children and grandchildren.

Remember the day at Horeb when you stood in front of Yahweh your God. He told me, ‘Bring the people together, and I will let them hear what I say. Then they will learn to revere me for life and show their children how.’
You came forward and stood at the foot of the mountain. It was burning, with flames shooting up to the sky itself, and darkness, cloud, and heavy gloom around it.
Yahweh spoke to you from inside the fire. Words reached your ears, but nothing reached your eyes. You heard a voice, nothing more.
He announced his covenant to you and told you to keep it: the Ten Words.{b} He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that same time Yahweh told me to teach you laws and rulings, to be followed in the land you are about to enter and own.
“Take great care of yourselves, then. When Yahweh addressed you at Horeb from the flames, you were not shown any shape at all.
So do not corrupt yourselves by carving an image in any form, be it a man, a woman,
a land animal, a flying bird,
a creature that crawls along the earth, or a fish in the waters beneath the land.

And when you lift your gaze to the sky and notice the sun, the moon, and the stars, the whole army of the sky, do not let yourselves be drawn into worshiping and serving them. Yahweh your God has assigned them to every people under heaven.
You, however, Yahweh took and rescued from Egypt, that blazing iron furnace, to be a people that belong to him, as you are now.
Because of you, Yahweh was furious with me and swore that I would never cross the Jordan or set foot in the good land Yahweh your God hands you as your own.
Here in this country I will die, not crossing the Jordan. You, though, are about to cross it and take that good land.
Do not lose sight of the covenant Yahweh your God has made with you. Make no idol in any shape that Yahweh your God has banned.
Yahweh your God is a devouring fire, a God who tolerates no rivals.

“Suppose that after you have had children and grandchildren, and been in the land a long time, you ruin yourselves by making an idol of any kind. You do evil in Yahweh your God’s eyes and make him angry.

As my witnesses against you today I name heaven and earth: you will soon vanish from the country you are crossing the Jordan to take. Your days there will be few, and you will be destroyed completely.
Yahweh will spread you out among the peoples. A small number of you will survive in the nations where Yahweh drives you.
There you will worship gods that people made, pieces of wood and stone with no sight, hearing, appetite, or sense of smell.
Yet from there you will look for Yahweh your God, and if you search with all your heart and all your being, you will find him.
When you are suffering, and all this has come upon you in days ahead, you will turn back to Yahweh your God and listen to him.
Since Yahweh your God shows mercy, he will not leave you, will not wipe you out, and will not forget the covenant he swore to your forefathers.

“Ask now about times long gone, before your own, from the day God made humankind{c} on earth, and from one end of the sky to the other. Has anything as great as this ever happened? Has anyone ever heard of the like?
Did any people hear a god{d} speak from a fire, as you did, and survive?

Has any god dared to come and pull one nation out from another? He did it with tests, signs, wonders, and war, with a mighty arm held out, and with terrifying deeds. All that Yahweh your God did in Egypt, you saw.
This was all shown to you so that you would know it: Yahweh alone is God, and nothing else compares.
He let you hear his voice from heaven so that you would be instructed. Down here he let you see his enormous fire, and from the middle of it his words reached you.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants, and with his own presence{e} and great power he led you out of Egypt.
Nations larger and mightier than you he cleared away in front of you, so that he could bring you in and hand you their land as your inheritance. That is how things stand now.
So understand today, and take it to heart, that Yahweh is God in the sky above and on the earth below. There is no other.
Keep his laws and commands, which I give you today, so that all goes well for you and your children after you, and so you stay a long time in the land Yahweh your God is giving you forever.”
Then Moses chose three cities east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Someone who killed a neighbor accidentally, with no earlier hatred, could run to one of these and live.
They were Bezer, in the desert on the plateau, for Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead for Gad; and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh.{f}
This is the teaching{g} Moses laid before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, laws, and rulings Moses gave them after they left Egypt,
It was in the valley facing Beth Peor, in the territory of Sihon, the Amorite king who reigned from Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites had overcome him on their way out of Egypt.
They seized his land, and also that of Og, king of Bashan. These two Amorite kings had ruled on the Jordan’s eastern side, toward sunrise.
It reached from Aroer, on the rim of the Arnon Gorge, to Mount Sion{h} (that is, Hermon),
and took in the whole Arabah east of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.

notes.text: Baal Peor means “lord of Peor.” See Numbers 25:1-9.
Hebrew “the ten words,” the Ten Commandments (also 10:4). See 5:6-21.
Or “Adam.” Hebrew adam means “humankind” and is also the name of the first man.
Or “the voice of God.” The Greek Old Testament reads “the voice of the living God.”
Hebrew “with his face.”
Bezer means “fortress”; Ramoth means “heights”; Golan may mean “circle” or “exile.” Gilead may mean “heap of witness” (Genesis 31:47-48).
Or “law.” Hebrew torah, “teaching.”
Hebrew Sion, a different name from Zion in Jerusalem. The Syriac reads “Sirion” (compare 3:9).

subheads.41: Cities of Refuge East of the Jordan

verses.text: Moses called all Israel together and told them, “Israel, hear the laws and rulings I am reciting in your ears today. Learn them and make sure you carry them out.
At Horeb, Yahweh our God made a covenant with us.
Yahweh did not seal this covenant with our ancestors but with us, every one of us here and alive now.
Yahweh spoke to you face to face on the mountain, from inside the fire.
(In those days I stood in the gap between Yahweh and you, relaying his word, since the fire terrified you and you refused to climb the mountain.) This is what he said:
‘I am Yahweh your God, the one who led you out of Egypt, where you lived as slaves.{a}
‘You will have no other gods in my presence.{b}
‘Do not make yourself an idol, any likeness{c} of what is in the sky up high, on the ground down low, or in the water beneath the land.

You will not bow to them or serve them. I, Yahweh your God, am a God who tolerates no rival. Where parents hate me, I bring their wrong back on their children, and on the third and fourth generations,
but to those who love me and keep my commands I show faithful love{d} through a thousand generations.{e}
‘You will not misuse the name of Yahweh your God.{f} Yahweh will not leave unpunished anyone who misuses his name.
‘Observe the Sabbath{g} day by treating it as holy, as Yahweh your God ordered you.
You have six days for your labor and all your work.

The seventh day, however, belongs to Yahweh your God as a Sabbath. On it no work may be done by you, your son or daughter, your slave, male or female, your ox, your donkey, or any animal of yours, or by the foreigner who lives in your towns. Your slaves, men and women, are to rest the same as you.
Do not forget that you were slaves in Egypt, and Yahweh your God brought you out with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That is why Yahweh your God has told you to keep the Sabbath.{h}
‘Honor your father and your mother, as Yahweh your God ordered you. In this way your life will be long and prosperous in the country Yahweh your God is giving you.{i}
‘You will not murder.{j}
‘You will not commit adultery.
‘You will not steal.
‘You will not give false testimony against your neighbor.{k}
‘You will not covet your neighbor’s wife. You will not long for your neighbor’s house or field, or his slaves, men or women, or his ox or donkey, or anything at all of his.’{l}

“These are the words Yahweh spoke to your entire gathering at the mountain, out of fire, cloud, and deep darkness, in a loud voice. He added nothing. Then he wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from the darkness, with the mountain burning, all your tribal heads and elders came to me.
You said, ‘Yahweh our God has let us see his glory and his greatness, and we heard his voice speak out of the fire. Today we have learned that God may talk with human beings, and they go on living.
But now why should we die? That huge fire will burn us up. If we hear Yahweh our God’s voice any longer, we will die.
Has any human{m} ever listened to the living God talk from the midst of a fire, as we have, and survived?
You go closer and listen to everything Yahweh our God says. Then tell us all that he says to you. We will listen and do it.’
“Yahweh heard what you said to me. He told me, ‘The words these people spoke to you reached me, and they have spoken well.
I wish their hearts would stay this way, fearing me and obeying every command of mine. Then they and their descendants would flourish for all time!
Now go and tell them to head back to their tents.
You, though, remain here with me. I will give you the entire command, the laws and rulings you must teach them, so that they can live by them in the country I am handing over to them.’
So take care to do exactly what Yahweh your God commanded you. Do not veer to the right or the left.
Follow the entire path Yahweh your God has set for you, so you will live, do well, and enjoy long life in the land you will own.”

notes.text: Verses 6-21 give the Ten Words (4:13) in a form close to Exodus 20:2-17. The main differences are noted at verses 12, 15, 16, 20, and 21.
Or “besides me” or “in addition to me”; Hebrew “before my face.”
Exodus 20:4 reads “or any likeness.” The Hebrew here lacks “or.”
Hebrew hesed, loyal and faithful love, especially within a covenant.
Or “to thousands.”
Or “in vain” or “to deceive”; Hebrew “lift up the name ... to emptiness.”
Exodus 20:8 reads “Remember the Sabbath day.” Sabbath means “ceasing” or “rest.”
Exodus 20:11 gives a different reason: Yahweh rested on the seventh day of creation. Here the reason is Israel’s release from slavery.
The words “as Yahweh your God ordered you” and “things will go well for you” are not in Exodus 20:12.
Hebrew ratsah, the unlawful killing of a person.
Hebrew shaw, “empty” or “worthless”; Exodus 20:16 has sheqer, “false.”
Exodus 20:17 puts the neighbor’s house first. Here the wife comes first, and “field” is added.
Hebrew “who of all flesh.”

verses.text: “This is the command, with its laws and rulings, that Yahweh your God told me to teach you, so you can follow it in the land you are about to enter and own.
It means that all your lives you will revere Yahweh your God and keep all his laws and commands that I am giving to you, to your children, and to your grandchildren, so that you may have a long life.
Listen up, Israel, and be sure to obey. That way you will prosper and multiply in a land flowing with milk and honey, exactly as Yahweh, the God your ancestors worshiped, promised you.{a}
“Hear,{b} Israel: Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone.{c}
You are to love Yahweh your God using all of your heart,{d} all of your life,{e} and all of your strength.{f}
Keep these words I am giving you today in your heart.
Repeat them to your children. Speak of them at home and on the road, at bedtime and at rising.
Tie them on your hand as a sign, and wear them on your forehead as a band.{g}
Write them on the doorposts{h} of your houses and on your gates.

“Yahweh your God is about to bring you into the land he swore to give you, the land promised to your forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Its cities are big and handsome, and you built none of them.
You will find houses stocked with every good thing you never stocked, wells you never dug, vineyards and olive trees you never planted. After you eat your fill,
take care not to forget Yahweh, who led you out of Egypt, the house of slavery.
Revere Yahweh your God, serve him, and when you take an oath, make it in his name only.
Do not chase after other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
Yahweh your God lives among you, and he tolerates no rival. If you turn away, his anger will blaze against you and wipe you off the earth.
Never try Yahweh your God’s patience the way you did at Massah.{i}
Keep carefully all the commands, instructions, and laws Yahweh your God has given you.
Do what is right and good in Yahweh’s eyes. Then all will go well, and you will go in and take the good land Yahweh swore to your ancestors,
forcing out all your enemies in front of you, as Yahweh promised.
“Someday your child will ask, ‘What do these instructions, laws, and rulings that Yahweh our God gave you mean?’
Then you will answer, ‘We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and Yahweh rescued us from Egypt with a powerful hand.
We watched as Yahweh sent great and terrible signs and wonders upon Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon every member of his household.
Then he took us out of there in order to lead us in and hand us the land he had sworn to our ancestors.
Yahweh ordered us to obey all these laws and to revere Yahweh our God, for our good always and to keep us alive, as he has done to this day.
If we are careful to keep every part of this command before Yahweh our God, as he ordered us, that will be our righteousness.’

notes.text: The Greek Old Testament adds, “These are the rulings and judgments Yahweh gave the Israelites in the wilderness after they left Egypt.”
Hebrew shema, “hear” or “listen and obey.” Jewish tradition calls verses 4-9 the Shema.
Or “Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one,” or “Yahweh is our God, Yahweh is one.” The Hebrew has no verb. The Greek Old Testament reads “The Lord our God is one Lord,” the form quoted in Mark 12:29.
Hebrew lebab, the center of thought, will, and feeling. The Greek Old Testament has “mind.”
Or “your whole soul” or “your life.”
Hebrew meod, literally “muchness,” meaning all your power and resources.
Hebrew totaphot, a word of uncertain meaning. Later Jewish practice read this as tefillin, small boxes holding these words, worn on the arm and forehead.
Hebrew mezuzot. The small case holding these words, fixed to a doorpost, is called a mezuzah.
Massah means “testing” (Exodus 17:7).

verses.text: “Yahweh your God will bring you into the country you are about to own, and he will remove great nations ahead of you. There are seven, each larger and stronger than you: Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
When Yahweh your God hands them to you and you defeat them, put them under the ban.{a} Make no treaty with them, and show them no pity.
Do not intermarry with them. Your daughters must not marry their sons, and their daughters must not marry yours,
for they would turn your children away from me to serve other gods. Then Yahweh’s anger would burn against you and quickly destroy you.
Treat them this way instead: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles,{b} and burn their idols.
You belong to Yahweh your God as a holy people. Out of every people on earth, he chose you to be his personal treasure.
It was not your size that made Yahweh fix his love on you and choose you, since you were the smallest of all peoples.
He did it because he loved you and wanted to keep the oath he swore to your ancestors. That is why Yahweh rescued you with a mighty hand, buying you out of slavery, from Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
So understand that Yahweh your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and faithful love for a thousand generations toward those who love him and keep his commands,
yet who repays to their faces those who hate him, by destroying them. He does not put off the one who hates him. He repays him face to face.
So obey the command, the laws, and the rulings I give you today.
“If you listen to these rulings and follow them with care, Yahweh your God will honor the covenant and faithful love he swore to your ancestors.

Love, blessing, and growth in numbers will come from him. Your children will be blessed, along with your crops, grain, wine, and oil, and the calves and lambs of your herds and flocks, in the land he swore to your forefathers that he would give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. Among you no man or woman will be without children, and none of your animals will be barren.
Yahweh will take every sickness away from you. The terrible diseases of Egypt that you know so well he will not put on you. He will inflict them on all who hate you instead.
Every people that Yahweh your God delivers to you, you must wipe out. Pity them not, and serve not their gods, since that would be a snare for you.
“You may be thinking, ‘They outnumber us. There is no way we can push them out.’
Do not let them frighten you. Think back to what Yahweh your God did to Pharaoh and the whole of Egypt:
the great trials your eyes saw, the signs, the wonders, and the mighty arm held out, by which Yahweh your God freed you. He will do exactly this to all the peoples you now fear.
Yahweh your God will also send the hornet{c} against them, until those who survive and hide from you are gone.
Do not be terrified of them, because Yahweh your God is with you, a great and awesome God.
Little by little, Yahweh your God will clear these nations from your path. You cannot wipe them out all at once, or the wild animals would grow too numerous for you.
Yahweh your God will turn them over to you and send them into a wild panic until they are all gone.
Their kings he will place in your hands, and you will blot their names out from under the sky. None will be able to stand against you until you have finished them.
Burn the carved images of their gods. Do not covet the silver and gold on them or take it for yourselves, or it will become a trap, because Yahweh your God finds it detestable.{d}
Do not bring anything detestable into your house, or you will be put under the ban, like it. Loathe it and treat it as filth, because it is under the ban.”

notes.text: Hebrew herem, “ban,” meaning something set apart for Yahweh and given up to destruction.
Wooden poles or trees associated with the goddess Asherah.
Or “panic” or “plague”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain. The Greek Old Testament has “hornets.”
Hebrew toebah, something abhorrent, especially in worship.

verses.text: “Follow carefully every command I give you today, so that you will live, grow in number, and enter and own the land Yahweh promised your ancestors.

Remember every mile Yahweh your God has led you across the wilderness over these forty years. He meant to humble and test you, to learn what lay in your heart, and whether you would keep his commands.

He humbled you by allowing hunger, and then fed you manna,{a} a food neither you nor your ancestors had ever known. This taught you that people cannot live on bread alone. They live on whatever Yahweh says.
In these forty years your clothes never wore out and your feet never swelled.
Understand in your heart that Yahweh your God corrects you as a father corrects his son.
So keep the commands of Yahweh your God, walk in his ways, and revere him.
Yahweh your God is taking you into a good country, one with streams and springs, with water rising from the depths in valleys and on hills,
a country with wheat, barley, grapevines, figs, pomegranates, olive trees, and honey,{b}
where food will never be scarce and you will lack nothing, where the rocks hold iron and you can dig copper from the hills.
You will eat and be full, and you will praise Yahweh your God for the good land he gave you.
“Take care not to forget Yahweh your God by ignoring the commands, rulings, and laws I give you today.
When you have eaten and are full, when you have built fine houses and settled in,
when your herds and flocks have grown large, your silver and gold have piled up, and all you own has increased,
do not let pride fill your heart and make you forget Yahweh your God, who rescued you from Egypt, the house of slavery.
He guided you through that vast and terrible desert, with its fiery{c} snakes and scorpions and its dry, waterless ground. Out of flint rock he made water flow for you.
In the wilderness he fed you manna, a food your ancestors had never known, to humble you and test you, so that in the end it would go well for you.
Never tell yourself, ‘My strength and my own hands made me rich.’
Remember Yahweh your God. It is he who gives you strength to earn wealth, to make his covenant, sworn to your ancestors, stand firm, as it stands today.
If you ever forget Yahweh your God, run after other gods, and bow down and serve them, then I give you a solemn warning today: you will surely be destroyed.
Like the nations Yahweh is destroying ahead of you, you will be destroyed, because you did not obey Yahweh your God.”

notes.text: Manna is probably named from the question “What is it?” (Exodus 16:15).
Probably both bees’ honey and the thick syrup made from dates or grapes.
Hebrew saraph, “burning,” perhaps from the painful bite of these snakes (Numbers 21:6).

verses.text: “Listen, Israel. Today you cross the Jordan to push out nations larger and stronger than yourselves, whose cities are huge, with walls that seem to touch the sky.
The people are big and tall, descendants of the Anakim. You know of them, and you have heard the saying, ‘Who can stand up to Anak’s sons?’

Be certain of this today: Yahweh your God is the one crossing ahead of you, like a fire that devours. He will wipe them out and bring them to their knees in front of you. You will drive them out and finish them quickly, as Yahweh promised.

Once Yahweh your God has shoved them from your path, never tell yourselves, ‘It was my own goodness that led Yahweh to bring me in and give me this country.’ No. These nations are wicked, and that is why Yahweh is driving them off ahead of you.

It is not your goodness or your honest heart that takes you in to own their land. Their wickedness is the reason Yahweh your God is driving them out, and he is also keeping the promise he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your ancestors.
Understand this: Yahweh your God is not handing you this good country because you deserve it. You are a stubborn people.
“Remember this and never forget it: in the wilderness you made Yahweh your God furious. You have rebelled against Yahweh from the day you left Egypt right up to your arrival here.
Even at Horeb you made Yahweh angry, so angry that he was ready to destroy you.
I had climbed the mountain to receive the stone tablets of the covenant Yahweh had made with you. For forty days and nights I stayed up there, eating no bread and drinking no water.
Yahweh gave me two stone tablets inscribed by God’s own finger. On them were all the words Yahweh had spoken to you from the fire on the mountain on the day you gathered.
When the forty days and nights ended, Yahweh gave me the two tablets of the covenant.
Then he said, ‘Go down at once. The people you led out of Egypt have done evil. They have quickly turned from the way I commanded and made themselves a metal idol.’
Yahweh went on, ‘I have been watching these people, and they are stubborn.
Leave me alone. I will destroy them and erase their name from under heaven, and I will make you into a nation larger and stronger than theirs.’
“I turned and went down the burning mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.
There you were, having sinned against Yahweh your God! You had cast a calf for yourselves. You had left the way Yahweh commanded so fast!
Gripping the two tablets, I hurled them out of my hands and shattered them as you looked on.
Then I threw myself down before Yahweh for forty days and nights again, with no bread and no water, because of all the sins you had committed, doing evil in his sight and provoking his anger.
I dreaded the rage and fury Yahweh felt toward you, enough to destroy you. Yet once again he gave me a hearing.
With Aaron,{a} too, Yahweh was so furious that he meant to destroy him, and so I interceded for Aaron as well, in those days.
That sinful thing you had made, the calf, I seized and burned in a fire. Then I pounded it, grinding it down until it was fine dust, and tossed the dust into the stream coming down off the mountain.
Taberah,{b} Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah{c} were three more places where you provoked Yahweh.
When Yahweh dispatched you from Kadesh Barnea with the order, ‘Go up and take the country I am giving you,’ you defied him. You neither trusted him nor listened to him.
You have rebelled against Yahweh as long as I have known you.{d}
“So I lay on my face before Yahweh those forty days and nights, since Yahweh had said he would destroy you.
I begged him, ‘Lord Yahweh, do not destroy your people, the ones who are your own, whom you bought back by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Think of your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Ignore how stubborn these people are, and their wickedness and sin.
Otherwise the country you brought us from will say, “Yahweh could not bring them to the land he promised, and he hated them, so he took them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
They are your people, your own, whom you brought out with your great power and outstretched arm.’

notes.text: The meaning of Aaron’s name is uncertain; it may be Egyptian.
Taberah means “burning” (Numbers 11:1-3).
Kibroth Hattaavah means “graves of craving” (Numbers 11:34).
The Greek Old Testament reads “from the day he became known to you.”

verses.text: “At that time Yahweh said to me, ‘Chisel out two new stone tablets, matching the first, then climb the mountain to meet me. Also construct a wooden chest.{a}
On the tablets I will inscribe what was written on the first pair, the pair you smashed. Then place them inside the chest.’
I made a chest from acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first, and carried them up the mountain.
He inscribed the tablets exactly as before, with the Ten Words he had spoken to you out of the fire on the mountain the day you were gathered there. Then Yahweh handed the tablets over to me.
I went back down and put the tablets into the chest I had made, and they are there now, as Yahweh ordered me.
(The Israelites left the wells of Beeroth Bene Jaakan{b} and went to Moserah.{c} At Moserah Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar{d} took over his priestly duties.
They marched on to Gudgodah and then to Jotbathah, a country of flowing streams.{e}
It was then that Yahweh chose the tribe of Levi{f} to carry the chest of Yahweh’s covenant, to stand before him and serve him, and to give blessings in his name, as they still do.
That is why Levi has no territory like his brothers. Yahweh himself is Levi’s inheritance, as Yahweh your God told him.)
“As on the first occasion, I spent forty days and forty nights on the mountain, and again Yahweh gave me a hearing. He chose not to destroy you.
‘Get going,’ Yahweh told me. ‘Take the lead and bring the people on their way, so they may enter and possess the land I promised their ancestors.’
“So now, Israel, here is all Yahweh your God wants of you: that you revere him, follow all his paths, love him, and serve him with your whole heart and being.
Keep Yahweh’s commands and laws that I give you today, for your own good.
The sky belongs to Yahweh your God, even the highest heavens, and so does the earth and everything on it.
Yet Yahweh set his heart on your ancestors and loved them. From all the peoples he chose their descendants, you, as is clear today.
So open your hearts{g} and stop being stubborn.
For Yahweh your God is God above all gods, Lord above all lords, the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, who favors no one and cannot be bribed.
He defends orphans and widows, and he loves foreigners, giving them food and clothes.
You must love foreigners too, since you were foreigners in Egypt.
Revere Yahweh your God and serve him. Hold tight to him, and swear by his name.
He is your praise, and he is your God. You saw with your own eyes the great and awesome things he did for you.
Seventy people of your family went down to Egypt, and now Yahweh your God has made you countless, like the stars of heaven.

notes.text: Hebrew aron, “chest,” the word used for the chest of the covenant (verse 8).
Beeroth Bene Jaakan means “wells of the sons of Jaakan.” The Greek Old Testament reads “Beeroth of the sons of Jakim.”
Moserah may mean “discipline.” Numbers 33:30-38 lists these stops in another order and places Aaron’s death at Mount Hor.
Eleazar means “God has helped.”
Gudgodah may mean “cleft”; Jotbathah means “pleasantness.”
Levi probably means “joined” or “attached” (Genesis 29:34).
Hebrew “circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.”

verses.text: “Love Yahweh your God, and always obey what he requires: his laws, rulings, and commands.
Consider what your children could never have seen. I speak of the discipline Yahweh your God imposed, his greatness, his strong hand, his outstretched arm,
the signs and acts he did in Egypt to Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and to his whole country,
and how he treated Egypt’s army with its horses and chariots, making the Red Sea{a} waters roll over them while they were in pursuit of you. Yahweh finished them off, and they are gone to this day.
Think of what he did for you in the wilderness until you got here,

Consider too what he did to the brothers Dathan and Abiram,{b} sons of Eliab of the tribe of Reuben, when the earth opened wide in front of all Israel and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every creature that was theirs.
It was your own eyes that saw all the great things Yahweh did.
“Therefore obey each command I give you today. It will make you strong enough to go in and take the country you are crossing over to claim,
and it will bring you a long life in the land Yahweh swore to your forefathers and to their children after them, a land rich with milk and honey.
The country you are entering to claim is not like Egypt, which you left, where you scattered seed and watered it with your foot,{c} as though tending a vegetable plot.
The land you are crossing to take has hills and valleys and drinks rain from the sky.
Yahweh your God cares for it. His eyes rest on it all year long, from the first day of the year to the last.
“If you listen well to the commands I am giving you today, and love Yahweh your God and serve him wholeheartedly,
then I{d} will send your land its rain at the proper season, autumn showers and spring showers,{e} so you can bring in grain, wine, and oil.
Grass will grow in your pastures for your animals, and you will have plenty to eat.
Guard yourselves so your hearts are not tricked into turning aside to serve and worship other gods.
If you do, Yahweh’s anger will blaze against you. He will shut up the sky so there is no rain and the ground yields nothing, and you will soon vanish from the good land Yahweh is giving you.
“Lodge these words of mine in your heart and mind. Tie them to your hand as a sign, and wear them between your eyes as a band.
Teach them to your children by talking about them at home and on the road, at bedtime and at rising.
Write them on your doorposts and your gates,
and the days of you and your children will be many in the land Yahweh swore to your ancestors he would give them, as many as the days the sky is over the earth.
If you faithfully keep every part of this command I am giving you, loving Yahweh your God, following all his ways, and staying close to him,
then Yahweh will clear all these nations out ahead of you, and you will take the place of nations larger and stronger than you.
Wherever the sole of your foot lands will be yours. Your border will run from the desert and Lebanon eastward to the Euphrates River, and westward to the far sea.{f}
No one will stand against you. As he promised, Yahweh your God will make everyone in the land where you walk dread and fear you.
“See, I am setting a blessing and a curse before you today.
The blessing comes if you obey the commands of Yahweh your God that I give you today.
The curse comes if you disobey those commands and turn from the way I tell you today, to follow other gods you have never known.
When Yahweh your God leads you into the country you are going to own, you must pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.{g}
As you know, those mountains lie across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the country of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, near Gilgal, beside the great trees{h} of Moreh.{i}
Soon you will cross the Jordan to take the country Yahweh your God is handing you. When you own it and live in it,
be careful to follow all the laws and rulings I place before you today.”

notes.text: Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here probably the Gulf of Aqaba. See the note at 1:40.
Dathan may mean “belonging to a fountain” (uncertain); Abiram means “my father is exalted”; Eliab means “my God is father”; Reuben means “See, a son!” (Genesis 29:32). See Numbers 16.
Probably by opening and closing small irrigation channels with the foot, or by treading a water wheel.
So the Hebrew. The Greek Old Testament has “he will give.”
Hebrew “the early rain and the late rain”: the fall rains that soften the ground for plowing (October-November) and the spring rains that fill out the grain (March-April).
Hebrew “the sea behind,” the Mediterranean; Hebrew directions faced east.
Gerizim and Ebal stand on either side of Shechem; the meanings of their names are uncertain. See 27:11-13.
Or “oaks” or “terebinths.”
Moreh means “teacher.” Gilgal means “circle,” perhaps of stones.

verses.text: “These are the laws and rulings you must carefully follow in the country Yahweh, your ancestors’ God, has given you to own, for as long as you live on earth.
Completely wreck every site where the nations you are pushing out worshiped their gods, whether on tall mountains, on hills, or under any leafy tree.
Pull down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, set fire to their Asherah poles, hack to pieces the idols of their gods, and wipe out their names from that spot.
Yahweh your God must not be worshiped in their manner.
You are to look for the one place Yahweh your God will pick from all your tribes as the home{a} for his name, and that is where you will go.
Bring there your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tenths, your gifts set apart,{b} your promised offerings and freewill offerings, and the first young of your herds and flocks.
There, with Yahweh your God watching, you and your families will eat and celebrate everything you have done, because Yahweh your God has blessed you.
“Do not do as we are doing here today, where everyone follows his own idea of what is right,
because you have not yet arrived at the resting place and inheritance Yahweh your God is giving you.
Once you cross the Jordan and settle in the country Yahweh your God gives you as your inheritance, he will give you peace from all the enemies around you, and you will live without fear.

Then you will bring everything I order to the place Yahweh your God picks as the home of his name: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tenths, your gifts set apart, and the best of what you have promised to Yahweh.
There you will celebrate in the presence of Yahweh your God, you, your sons and daughters, your slaves of both sexes, and the Levite from your towns, who has no allotment of land among you.
Never offer your burnt offerings at any spot you happen to see.
Offer them only at the place Yahweh picks in one of your tribes, and do there all that I command you.

“Still, whenever you want, you may kill an animal and eat its meat in any of your towns, as much as Yahweh your God has blessed you with. Those who are clean and those who are not may both eat it, the way they eat gazelle or deer.
Only the blood is forbidden. Pour it onto the ground like water.

In your own towns you may not eat the tenth of your grain, wine, or oil, or the first young of your herds and flocks, or anything you have promised, or your freewill offerings, or your gifts set apart.

You must eat these in Yahweh your God’s presence, at the place he picks, with your children, your male and female slaves, and the Levites of your towns, celebrating before Yahweh your God in all you have worked for.
Never neglect the Levite as long as you live in your land.
“When Yahweh your God enlarges your territory, as he promised, and you crave meat and say, ‘I would like to eat some,’ you may eat as much as you wish.
If the place Yahweh your God picks for his name is too far from you, you may kill animals from the herds and flocks he gave you, as I have instructed, and eat in your own towns as much as you wish.
Eat it the way gazelle or deer is eaten. Anyone may have it, clean or unclean.
But hold firm on one point: you must not eat the blood. Blood is life, and life may not be eaten together with the flesh.
Do not eat it. Pour it on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that things go well for you and your children after you, because you are doing what Yahweh sees as right.
Only your sacred gifts and the things you have promised must you carry to the place Yahweh picks.
On the altar of Yahweh your God, offer your burnt offerings, both the flesh and the blood. For your other sacrifices, the blood is poured out beside the altar, while you eat the flesh.
Listen carefully to every one of these words I am giving you, so that all goes well for you and your children forever, because you are doing what is good and right in Yahweh your God’s sight.
“Yahweh your God will cut down the nations in front of you, and you will push them out and live in their land.
Once they have been destroyed, take care you are not snared into copying them. Never ask, ‘How did those nations serve their gods? I will follow their example.’ Do not do so.
You must not worship Yahweh your God in that way. They did for their gods every hateful thing Yahweh despises, even burning their own sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
“Do everything I command you. Add nothing to it, and take nothing from it.{c}

notes.text: Or “to put his name there, to make it dwell.” The Hebrew can be read either way.
Hebrew terumah, a portion “lifted” or set apart from one’s goods as an offering.
Verse 32 is 13:1 in the Hebrew text.

verses.text: “A prophet or dreamer may appear among you and promise a sign or wonder.{a}
The sign or wonder comes true, and he says, ‘Let us follow other gods,’ ones you have not known, ‘and serve them.’
Do not listen to that prophet or dreamer. Yahweh your God is testing you to learn whether you love him with all your heart and being.
Yahweh your God is the one to follow and revere. Keep his commands, heed his voice, serve him, and hold tight to him.

That prophet or dreamer must be put to death for urging rebellion against Yahweh your God, who led you out of Egypt and bought you out of slavery, and for trying to push you off the road Yahweh your God told you to take. This is how you will sweep evil out of your midst.

“Your brother, your mother’s own son, or your son or daughter, or the wife you cherish, or your closest friend may try to secretly lure you: ‘Let’s go and serve other gods,’ gods unknown to you and your ancestors,
They may be gods of peoples nearby or far away, anywhere on earth from end to end.
Do not give in to him or listen. Show no pity. Do not spare him or protect him.
You must kill him. Your hand will be the first against him, then the hands of everyone else.
Stone him to death, because he tried to drag you away from Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt, the house of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear, and fear will keep any of you from doing such evil again.
“Word may reach you that in one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you to live in
that some worthless men{b} from among you have misled the townspeople, saying, ‘Let’s go and serve other gods,’ ones you have not known.
Then look into it, question witnesses, and ask carefully. If the report is true and it is certain that this detestable act took place among you,
you must strike the people of that town with the sword. Put it under the ban, everything in it, even the animals, with the sword.
Collect all its goods in the middle of the public square and burn the town and all that is in it, as a whole offering{c} to Yahweh your God. It will stay a ruin forever and will never be rebuilt.
None of what is under the ban may stay in your hands. Then Yahweh will turn from his burning anger, pity you, treat you kindly, and make you numerous, as he swore to your forefathers,
provided you obey Yahweh your God, keep every command I give you today, and do what pleases him.”

notes.text: Verses 1-18 are numbered 2-19 in the Hebrew text.
Hebrew “sons of Belial,” an expression of uncertain origin for worthless or wicked people.
Hebrew kalil, “complete,” a word used for an offering that is entirely burned.

verses.text: “You are children of Yahweh your God. When someone dies, do not slash your skin or shave your forehead{a} in mourning,
because you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Out of all the peoples on earth, Yahweh chose you to be his own, his treasured people.
“Never eat anything detestable.
Here are the animals you are free to eat: the sheep, the goat, the ox,
the gazelle, the mountain sheep, the antelope, the ibex, the wild goat, the roebuck, and the red deer.{b}
You may eat any animal that has a hoof split into two parts and that also chews the cud.
But among animals that chew the cud or have split hooves, you may not eat the camel, hare, or rock badger.{c} They chew the cud but have no split hoof, so they are unclean for you.
The pig has a split hoof but does not chew the cud, so you must count it unclean. Their meat is not for your table, and their dead bodies must not be touched.
“Of everything that lives in water, you may eat whatever has fins and scales.
Anything that has no fins or scales is unclean for you and must stay off your table.
“You may eat any clean bird.
These you may not eat: the eagle,{d} the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the falcon, the kite in all its kinds,{e}
all the kinds of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, the hawk in all its kinds,
the barn owl, the little owl, the great owl,
the cormorant, the pelican, the carrion vulture,
the stork, the heron in all its kinds, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every swarming winged insect counts as unclean for you. None may be eaten.
Any clean winged creature may be eaten.

“Never eat anything found already dead. Give it to the foreigner in your town, or sell it to an outsider. You are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Never cook a kid goat in the milk of its own mother.
“Each year, put aside one tenth of all that your fields yield.

In the presence of Yahweh your God, at the place he picks as the home of his name, eat the tenth of your grain, wine, and oil, and the first young of your herds and flocks, so that you learn to always revere Yahweh your God.
If the trip is too long for you to carry it, because the place Yahweh your God picks for his name is far off, and Yahweh your God has blessed you,
turn it into silver. Take the silver with you to the place Yahweh your God picks.
With the silver, buy anything you like: oxen, sheep, wine, beer, anything at all. Eat there before Yahweh your God and enjoy yourselves, you and your household.
The Levite in your towns is not to be left out, since he has no allotment with you.
“Every third year, when it ends, bring the entire tenth of that year’s harvest and store it in your towns.

The Levite, who has no share or inheritance of land with you, and the foreigner, orphan, and widow in your towns may come, eat, and be satisfied. Then Yahweh your God will bless all the work of your hands.”

notes.text: Hebrew “make a baldness between your eyes.”
The identification of several of the animals in this verse is uncertain.
Hebrew shaphan, the rock hyrax.
Or “griffon vulture.” Many of the birds in verses 12-18 cannot be identified with certainty.
Hebrew lists three birds here, with the second and third written alike; Leviticus 11:14 has only two.

verses.text: “When seven years have passed, you are to cancel debts.{a}

Here is how it works: every lender must drop his claim on whatever he loaned a fellow Israelite. He may not press his neighbor or relative to repay, since a canceling in honor of Yahweh has been announced.
A foreigner you may press for payment, but any debt a fellow Israelite owes you, you must drop.
Still, nobody among you should be poor, since Yahweh will richly bless you in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to own as an inheritance,
so long as you pay close attention to Yahweh your God and carefully keep every part of this command I give you today.
Yahweh your God will bless you as he promised. Many nations will borrow from you, and you will borrow from none. Many nations will be under your rule, and none will rule you.
“If there is a needy person among you, a fellow Israelite in any town of the land Yahweh your God is giving you, do not turn hard-hearted or keep your fist closed against him.
Open your hand wide, and lend him freely whatever he needs to cover what he is lacking.

Beware of an ugly thought crossing your mind: ‘The seventh year, the year for canceling debts, is near.’ Then you would stare coldly at your needy relative and give him nothing. He might appeal to Yahweh about you, and you would carry the guilt.
Give to him generously and without grumbling in your heart. Because of this, Yahweh your God will bless you in all your labor and everything you try.
Poverty will never leave the land entirely. For that reason I am telling you to open your hand wide to your fellow Israelites, to the poor and needy in your country.
“A Hebrew, man or woman, may be sold to you. If so, he serves you six years, and in the seventh you will let him go free.
When you free him, do not send him away empty-handed.
Supply him lavishly from your flock, threshing floor, and winepress. Give in proportion to how Yahweh your God has blessed you.
Keep in mind that you were slaves in Egypt, and Yahweh your God bought your freedom. For that reason I am giving you this order now.
Suppose the slave says to you, ‘I do not want to go away from you.’ He may love you and your family and be well off with you.
Then take an awl and drive it through his earlobe into the door. From then on he is your slave for life. Do likewise with a female slave.
Do not resent setting him free. In six years he has earned you double what a hired worker would cost. And Yahweh your God will bless all you do.
“Every firstborn male of your herds and flocks must be dedicated to Yahweh your God. Do not make a firstborn ox work, and do not shear a firstborn sheep.
You and your household are to eat these animals each year before Yahweh your God, at the place Yahweh picks.
If one has a flaw, such as lameness, blindness, or some other serious defect, do not sacrifice it to Yahweh your God.
Eat it in your own towns. Clean and unclean people may share it, as with gazelle or deer.
Just do not eat the blood. Let it drain onto the ground like water.

notes.text: Hebrew shemittah, a “letting drop,” here the cancellation or suspension of debts.

verses.text: “Keep the month of Abib (March-April){a} by celebrating the Passover for Yahweh your God, since it was in Abib, at night, that Yahweh your God led you out of Egypt.
Sacrifice the Passover animal to Yahweh your God, from your flock or herd, at the place where Yahweh picks to make his name live.
Eat no leavened bread with it. Eat unleavened bread, the bread of suffering, for seven days, because you left Egypt in a hurry. Then you will remember all your days the time you left Egypt.
For seven days, no yeast may be seen anywhere in your land, and no meat from the evening sacrifice of the first day may remain until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in whichever of your towns Yahweh your God gives you.
You will sacrifice it only at the place where Yahweh your God picks to make his name live, in the evening at sunset,{b} the hour you left Egypt.
Cook and eat it at the place Yahweh your God picks, and next morning you may head back to your tents.
Eat unleavened bread for six days. The seventh day is a holy gathering for Yahweh your God, and you do no work on it.
“Count seven weeks, beginning when the sickle first touches the standing grain.
Then hold the Feast of Weeks{c} for Yahweh your God, bringing a freewill gift from your own hand, as much as Yahweh your God has blessed you.

Celebrate before Yahweh your God at the place he picks to make his name live. Bring your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite from your town, and the foreigner, orphan, and widow among you.
Remember you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to keep these laws.
“Hold the Feast of Booths{d} for seven days, once you have brought in the produce of your threshing floor and winepress.
Rejoice at the feast with your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite, foreigner, orphan, and widow from your towns.
For seven days hold this feast for Yahweh your God at the place he chooses, because Yahweh your God will bless your whole harvest and all your work, and your happiness will be complete.

Three times a year every man among you must appear before Yahweh your God at the place he picks: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths. No one may come before Yahweh empty-handed.
Each person brings what he is able, according to the blessing Yahweh your God has given him.
“Appoint judges and officers for every town Yahweh your God gives you, tribe by tribe, to judge the people fairly.
Never twist justice or play favorites. Take no bribes, since a bribe makes wise people blind and bends the words of the honest.
Chase after justice, only justice, so you can live and own the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
“Beside the altar you build for Yahweh your God, you must not plant a tree of any kind as an Asherah pole,
and you must not set up a sacred pillar, which Yahweh your God hates.

notes.text: Hebrew “the month of Abib” (“ear of grain”), the month when the barley ripened, later called Nisan. It is the first month of the year counted from spring (Exodus 12:2; 13:4). The Hebrew calendar follows the moon, so the modern equivalent is approximate.
Hebrew “in the evening, at the going down of the sun.” Exodus 12:6 has the lamb slaughtered “between the two evenings,” that is, at twilight.
Hebrew Shavuot, later also called Pentecost, held seven weeks after Passover, in the third month, Sivan (May-June).
Or “Tabernacles” (Hebrew Sukkot), held in the seventh month, Tishri (September-October); see Leviticus 23:34.

verses.text: “Never sacrifice to Yahweh your God an ox or sheep with any flaw or defect, because Yahweh your God finds that detestable.
“A man or woman may be discovered in one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight by breaking his covenant.
That person has gone off to serve and bow to other gods, such as the sun, the moon, or the army of the sky, which I forbade.
Word of it reaches you. Then look into it thoroughly. If it proves to be so, and this hateful act has really been done in Israel,
take the guilty man or woman to the gates of your town and stone that person until dead.
A person may be executed only if two or three witnesses testify. A single witness is never enough for a death sentence.
The witnesses throw the first stones, and afterward everyone else joins in. In this way you burn the evil out of your midst.
“Some case in your towns may be too difficult for you to decide, such as one over bloodshed, a legal claim, or an injury. Then go up to the place Yahweh your God picks.
Go before the Levite priests and the judge in office at that time. Inquire, and they will announce the verdict.
You must then do as they decide, at that place Yahweh picks. Take care to follow all their directions.
Follow the teaching they give you and the decision they announce. Do not stray from what they tell you, to the left or to the right.
Whoever is so arrogant as to ignore the priest serving there for Yahweh your God, or the judge, must die. You will burn the evil out of Israel.
Everyone will hear of it and fear, and nobody will dare to be so bold again.
“After you enter the land Yahweh your God is giving you, take it, and settle there, you may say, ‘We want a king to rule us, like all the nations around us.’
You may certainly appoint a king, provided Yahweh your God chooses him. He has to come from among your own people. Never place a foreigner over yourselves.
The king must not collect many horses or send people to Egypt to buy more, since Yahweh has told you, ‘Never return that way.’
He must not gather many wives, or his heart will wander. He must not stockpile huge amounts of silver and gold.
When he takes his seat on the royal throne, he must write out for himself a copy of this teaching{a} on a scroll, using the one the Levite priests keep.
He is to keep it with him and read from it every day of his life. That will teach him to revere Yahweh his God and to carefully obey every word of this teaching and these laws,
so that he does not think he is better than his own people or turn aside from the command to the left or right. Then he and his sons will reign long over Israel.”

notes.text: Hebrew torah, “teaching” or “law.” The Greek Old Testament renders “a copy of this law” as deuteronomion touto, “this second law,” from which the book’s English name, Deuteronomy, comes.

verses.text: “The Levite priests, the entire tribe of Levi, will receive no land allotment in Israel. Their food will be the gifts{a} given to Yahweh by fire, which are their inheritance.
They will own no land among their relatives. Yahweh himself is their inheritance, exactly as he told them.
This is what the priests are owed by people who bring a sacrificial ox or sheep: the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
You will also give the priest the first of your grain, wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your sheep.
Yahweh your God has picked him and his descendants from all your tribes to serve in Yahweh’s name always.
“A Levite may leave any town of Israel where he lives and come, as eagerly as he likes, to the place Yahweh picks.
He may then serve in the name of Yahweh his God like all the other Levites who serve there in Yahweh’s presence.
He receives an equal share of food, apart from whatever he gets from selling what his family owns.{b}
“Once you have entered the land Yahweh your God is giving you, never learn the hateful customs of those nations.
Nobody among you may burn a son or daughter as an offering, or practice divination, fortune telling, omen reading, or witchcraft,
or cast spells, or ask advice from mediums and spirits, or call up the dead.
Whoever does these things is hateful to Yahweh. Because of such practices Yahweh your God is pushing those nations out in front of you.
You must be wholly loyal to Yahweh your God.
The nations you are about to replace pay attention to sorcerers and diviners. But Yahweh your God has not allowed you to do the same.
“From among your own people Yahweh your God will raise up for you a prophet like me. Listen to him.
It is just what you begged of Yahweh your God at Horeb, the day you were assembled: ‘Please let us not hear Yahweh our God’s voice again or look at this huge fire again, or we will die.’
Yahweh told me, ‘They are right in what they said.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you, a countryman of theirs, put my words into his mouth, and have him tell them whatever I order.
Anyone who disregards what this prophet says in my name will answer to me personally.
But any prophet who has the nerve to speak a message in my name that I did not order, or who speaks for other gods, must die.’
You may ask yourself, ‘How will we know that Yahweh has not spoken a message?’
Suppose a prophet speaks in Yahweh’s name and the message never happens or proves true. Then Yahweh did not speak it. The prophet said it out of arrogance. Do not be afraid of him.”

notes.text: Hebrew isshe, offerings presented by fire or as food gifts; the exact sense is debated.
The Hebrew is obscure; literally “besides his sales by the fathers.”

subheads.1: Gifts for the Priests and Levites

verses.text: “Yahweh your God will wipe out the nations whose land he is giving you. After you have pushed them out and moved into their cities and houses,
choose three towns for yourselves inside the land Yahweh your God is giving you as your own.
Make roads leading to them, and divide the country Yahweh your God gives you into three districts, so that anyone who kills a person can run to a town.
Here is the rule for a killer who runs there to save his life: the death of his neighbor must have been an accident, with no earlier hatred.

For instance, two men go into the woods to chop wood. One swings his axe at a tree, the blade slips off the handle, and it hits the other man, who dies. The one who swung may flee to one of these towns and live.

Without these towns, the relative responsible for avenging blood{a} might chase him down in a burning rage, since the journey is long, and kill him, though he did not deserve to die, as he had no earlier hatred for the dead man.
That is why I order you to choose three towns.
If Yahweh your God enlarges your territory as he swore to your ancestors, and hands over the whole country he promised them,
as long as you carefully follow this whole command that I give you today, loving Yahweh your God and always walking in his ways, you will add three more towns to these three.
That way, no innocent blood will be spilled in the land Yahweh your God gives you as your inheritance, and you will not be guilty of bloodshed.
“Suppose instead that a man hates his neighbor, hides and waits for him, jumps him and kills him, and then escapes to one of these towns.
The elders of his hometown must send men to bring him back and hand him over to the avenger of blood to be killed.
Have no pity on him. You must clear Israel of the guilt of innocent blood so that you will prosper.
“Do not shift the boundary stone that marks your neighbor’s land, put there long ago by earlier generations, on the property you will receive in the country Yahweh your God is giving you.
“One witness alone cannot convict anyone of any crime or wrongdoing. A charge stands only when two or three witnesses support it.
A malicious witness may come forward and accuse someone of a crime.
Then both people in the dispute must appear before Yahweh, in front of the priests and judges serving at that time.
The judges must check carefully. If the witness proves to be a liar who made a false accusation against a fellow Israelite,
treat him exactly as he intended to treat the other man. You will burn the evil out of your midst.
The rest will hear of it and be afraid, and never again will such evil be done among you.
Show no pity. The penalty is life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.”

notes.text: Hebrew goel haddam, the relative responsible for avenging a kinsman’s death.

verses.text: “When you march out against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army bigger than yours, do not fear them, because Yahweh your God, who brought you up from Egypt, is with you.
Just before the battle, the priest must come forward and speak to the army.
He will say, ‘Listen, Israel. Soon you will be in battle with your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid or panic or shake before them,
