because Yahweh your God marches beside you. He will fight on your side against your enemies and rescue you.’
The officers will then say to the army, ‘Is there a man who has built a new house but never dedicated it? He should leave for home, or he may die in battle and another man dedicate it.
Is there a man who planted a vineyard but never ate from it? Let him go home, or death in battle may give another man its harvest.
Is there a man engaged to a woman who is not yet his wife? Let him go home, or he may fall in battle and another man take her.’
The officers will add, ‘Is anyone afraid and discouraged? He may go home, so he does not make his fellow soldiers lose heart as well.’
When the officers finish speaking, they will name commanders to lead the army.
“As you approach a town to attack it, first offer peace.
If the people agree and open the gates, all of them will work for you as forced laborers.
If they refuse peace and fight you, then lay siege to the town.
When Yahweh your God hands it over to you, kill every man in it with the sword.
Women, children, animals, and everything else in the town, all its spoils, you may take for yourselves. You may use the goods you take from enemies, which Yahweh your God has given you.
This is how to treat every town far from you, those that are not among the nearby nations.
In the towns of the peoples Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, however, you must not let anything that breathes survive.
Put every one of them under the ban:{a} Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Yahweh your God has given the order,
so that they cannot teach you the hateful acts they performed for their gods and lead you into sin against Yahweh your God.
“Say you surround a city for many days to take it. Never ruin its trees with an axe. You may eat their fruit, but leave them standing. Are trees in the field people, that you should besiege them?{b}
You may destroy and cut down only trees you know do not produce food, and use them to build siege works against the city at war with you until it falls.”

notes.text: Hebrew herem. See the note at 2:34. The Greek Old Testament adds “the Girgashites” (compare 7:1).
Or “for the tree of the field is man’s life.” The Hebrew is difficult.

verses.text: “A corpse may turn up lying in an open field in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to own, and nobody knows who killed the man.
Your elders and judges must go out and measure the distance from the body to the surrounding towns.
The elders of the town closest to the body must then take a young cow that has never been worked or pulled with a yoke.
They will lead it down to a valley with a stream that always runs, ground that has never been plowed or planted, and there, beside the stream, they will break its neck.
The Levite priests will step forward, since Yahweh your God has picked them to serve him and to bless people in Yahweh’s name. They decide every dispute and every case of assault.
The elders from the town closest to the dead man will then rinse their hands above the young cow whose neck was broken in the valley,
and they will say, ‘We did not spill this blood, and we saw nothing of it.
Yahweh, forgive your people Israel, whom you rescued, and do not hold the guilt of innocent blood against them.’ The bloodshed will then be forgiven them.
This is how you clear away the guilt of innocent blood from among you, by doing what is right in Yahweh’s eyes.
“Suppose you go to war with your enemies, Yahweh your God gives you the victory, and you bring home prisoners.
If you notice a beautiful woman among them, want her, and decide to marry her,
bring her to your home. She is to shave her head and cut her nails,
She is to take off the clothes she was wearing when captured and remain in your house, mourning her parents for a full month. Only then may you take her as your wife, and become her husband.
If she no longer pleases you, let her go wherever she wants. You may not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have shamed her.
“A man may have two wives, one loved and one unloved. Both bear him sons, but the first son born is the unloved wife’s.
When the man divides his property among his sons, he is not allowed to treat the loved wife’s son as firstborn in place of the unloved wife’s son, who really is the firstborn.
He must acknowledge the unloved wife’s son as firstborn and give him twice as much as any other son out of all he has. That son was the first sign of his strength, and the firstborn’s rights are his.
“A man may have a son who is stubborn and rebellious, who will not obey his father or mother, even when they punish him.
His parents are to grab him and haul him to the town elders, who sit at the gate.
They will tell the elders, ‘Our son here is stubborn and rebellious and ignores what we say. He is a glutton and a drunk.’
Then every man in town will stone him to death. You will burn the evil out of your midst, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
“A man may commit a crime that carries the death penalty, and you put him to death and hang his body on a tree.
Do not leave it hanging there overnight. Bury it the same day, since a hanged person is cursed by God.{a} Otherwise you would pollute the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.

notes.text: Or “an insult to God.” Galatians 3:13 quotes this verse in a form close to the Greek Old Testament.

verses.text: “If you see a fellow Israelite’s ox or sheep wandering off, do not act as though you did not notice. Return them to their owner without fail.
Perhaps the owner lives far away, or you cannot tell whose animal it is. Then take it home and keep it until he comes searching. Then return it to him.
Do the same with a donkey, a coat, or anything else a fellow Israelite loses and you find. Do not look away.
If you see a fellow Israelite’s donkey or ox collapsed on the road, do not walk past. Stay and help him raise it.
“A woman must not dress in men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothes. Yahweh your God finds anyone who does this detestable.
“A bird’s nest may lie along your path, with chicks or eggs inside and the mother sitting over them, whether it is in a tree or on the ground. Do not take her together with her young.
Take the young if you like, but release the mother. Do this so that things go well for you and your life is long.
“When you build a new house, surround the roof with a railing. Then no one can fall from it and make your household guilty of bloodshed.
“Do not sow your vineyard with a mixture of two seeds. If you do, the whole crop, both the seed you planted and the vineyard’s produce, is forfeited.{a}
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey harnessed together.
Do not wear clothes made from wool and linen woven together.
“Sew tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
“A man may marry a woman, sleep with her, and then come to dislike her.
He accuses her of shameful behavior and ruins her reputation. ‘I married this woman,’ he says, ‘but when we came together I discovered she was not a virgin.’
Then the young woman’s father and mother must take the proof of her virginity to the town elders at the gate.
Her father will tell the elders, ‘My daughter was given by me to this man as a wife, and now he hates her.
He has charged her with shameful behavior, claiming she was not a virgin. Yet this is my proof that she was.’ They then spread the cloth out before the town elders.
The elders will seize the man and discipline him.

The fine is 2½ pounds of silver,{b} paid to the young woman’s father, because the man ruined the reputation of an Israelite virgin. She remains his wife, and as long as he lives he is never allowed to divorce her.
But suppose the charge is true and no proof of her virginity can be found.

Then they will lead her to her father’s front door, where the men of her town will stone her until she dies. She did a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting like a prostitute while she lived in her father’s home. You will burn the evil out of your midst.
“A man may be caught in bed with another man’s wife. Both must die, the man who slept with her and the woman as well. You will clear the evil out of Israel.
“A virgin may be engaged to a man, and some other man comes upon her in town and lies down with her.

Bring both of them out to that town’s gate and stone them until they die. The woman is guilty because she did not scream though she was in town, and the man is guilty because he violated his neighbor’s wife. You will burn the evil out of your midst.
But suppose the man finds the engaged woman out in open country and forces her to lie with him. Then only the man is to die.
Do nothing to the woman. She has done nothing deserving death. This case is like one where a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.
The man found her in open country, and although the engaged woman screamed, nobody was there to save her.
“A man may find a virgin who is not engaged, take hold of her, and sleep with her, and they are discovered.
The man must give the young woman’s father 20 ounces of silver,{c} and she becomes his wife, since he dishonored her. He is never allowed to divorce her, not in all his life.
“A man may not marry his father’s wife and so uncover his father’s bed.{d}

notes.text: Hebrew “become holy,” that is, forfeited to the sanctuary.
Hebrew “a hundred of silver,” that is, 100 shekels, about 40 ounces or 1.15 kilograms.
Hebrew “fifty of silver,” that is, 50 shekels, about 20 ounces or 575 grams.
Hebrew “the edge of his father’s garment.” This verse is 23:1 in the Hebrew text. To uncover the skirt of the father is to violate his marriage; compare Ruth 3:9.

verses.text: “A man whose testicles are crushed or cut may not enter the assembly of Yahweh.{a}
Nobody born from a forbidden union{b} may enter Yahweh’s assembly, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter Yahweh’s assembly. Even their descendants through ten generations may never enter it.
They did not welcome you with food and water as you traveled out of Egypt, and they paid Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Aram Naharaim,{c} to curse you.
Yahweh your God refused to hear Balaam. In love for you, he changed the curse into a blessing.
For as long as you live, never seek peace or prosperity for them.
“Do not despise an Edomite, who is your relative. Do not despise an Egyptian, since you lived as a foreigner in his country.
Their great-grandchildren, the third generation born to them, may enter Yahweh’s assembly.
“When your army camps against enemies, keep yourselves away from anything evil.
A man among you may be unclean because of a nighttime emission. He must leave the camp and stay out.
Toward evening he bathes in water, and when the sun sets he may return to camp.
Set aside a spot outside the camp for use as a toilet.
Carry a small shovel with your gear. When you squat outside, dig a hole with it, then turn and cover your waste.
Yahweh your God travels with your camp to protect you and to hand your enemies over. Therefore the camp must stay holy. If he sees anything indecent among you, he will turn away.
“Do not return to his master a slave who has run away to you.
Let him stay among you, in any town he picks and any place he likes. Do not mistreat him.
“No Israelite woman or man may serve as a shrine prostitute.{d}
Do not bring the earnings of a prostitute, male or female,{e} into the house of Yahweh your God to pay any vow. Yahweh your God hates both.
“Do not charge fellow Israelites interest on loans of money, food, or anything else that earns interest.
You may charge interest to a foreigner, but not to a fellow Israelite. If you obey, Yahweh your God will bless all your work in the land you are about to enter and own.
“When you make a vow to Yahweh your God, do not delay paying it. Yahweh your God will surely demand it, and you would be guilty.
If you simply do not make a vow, you are not guilty.
Be careful to do whatever your lips have promised, as you freely vowed to Yahweh your God with your own mouth.
“In a neighbor’s vineyard you may eat grapes until you are full, as many as you wish, but none may go in your basket.
In your neighbor’s field of grain you may pick ears with your hand, but never use a sickle on his standing grain.

notes.text: Verses 1-25 here are numbered 2-26 in the Hebrew text.
Hebrew mamzer, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps one born of incest or of a marriage forbidden by the law.
Aram Naharaim means “Aram of the two rivers,” the region of upper Mesopotamia.
Hebrew qedeshah (feminine) and qadesh (masculine), literally “consecrated one.” The exact practice is debated.
Hebrew “a dog’s payment.” “Dog” probably refers to a male prostitute.

verses.text: “Say a man marries a woman and afterward is unhappy with her, having found something improper in her. He writes up divorce papers, gives them to her, and dismisses her from his home.
Once out of his home she becomes the wife of someone else.
Perhaps this second husband turns against her too, drawing up divorce papers, handing them over, and dismissing her. Or perhaps the second husband dies.

In either case, the first husband who dismissed her is forbidden to take her back as his wife, since she has been made unclean. That is detestable to Yahweh. Never bring guilt upon the land that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.
“A newly married man is not to go to war or be given any public duty. During a whole year he is free to remain at home and give joy to the wife he married.
“Do not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper one, as a pledge for a loan. That would mean taking away a person’s means of living.{a}
“Anyone caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and making him a slave or selling him must be put to death. You will burn the evil out of your midst.
“When a skin disease{b} breaks out, take great care to follow everything the Levite priests teach you. I gave them orders, and you must be careful to carry them out.
Remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam while you were traveling, after Egypt.
“When you lend your neighbor anything at all, do not go into his house to choose a pledge for yourself.
Stay outside. The man who borrowed from you will bring the pledge out to you.
If he is poor, do not go to bed with his pledge still in your hands.
Return it by sundown so he can sleep in his coat and thank you. Yahweh your God will count that as a righteous deed on your part.
“Never exploit a hired worker who is poor and needy, be he a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living in a town of yours.
Pay him each day’s wages before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry to Yahweh against you, and you will be guilty.
“Parents are not to be executed for crimes of their children, and children are not to be executed for crimes of their parents. Each person is executed only for his own sin.
“Do not deprive a foreigner or an orphan of fair treatment, and do not take a widow’s coat as a pledge.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and Yahweh your God bought you back from there. That is the reason I order you to do this.
“While harvesting your field, you may forget a bundle of grain. Do not go back for it. It belongs to the widow, the orphan, and the foreigner, and then Yahweh your God will bless all that you do.
After you have beaten the olives from your trees, do not search the branches again. What remains belongs to the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
After you have picked your vineyard, do not strip it a second time. What grapes remain are for the orphan, the widow, and the foreigner.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is my reason for this command.”

notes.text: Hebrew “life” (nephesh).
Hebrew tsaraat, traditionally “leprosy,” a term covering various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13-14.

verses.text: “Two men may have a dispute and take it to court, where the judges hear the case. They must acquit the one who is right and condemn the one who is wrong.
If the guilty man deserves a beating, the judge will order him down on the ground and have him flogged in the judge’s presence, up to the number of lashes his offense deserves.
He may receive up to forty lashes, no more. More than that would humiliate your fellow Israelite in front of you.
“Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out grain.

“Brothers may share a household, and one of them dies with no son. The widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother goes to her, makes her his wife, and does his duty as brother-in-law.{a}
The first son she bears will carry on the dead brother’s name, so that it is not wiped out of Israel.

But he may be unwilling to marry his brother’s widow. Then she goes to the elders at the town gate and says, ‘My husband’s brother will not keep his brother’s name alive in Israel. He refuses to do his duty as my brother-in-law.’
The town’s elders will summon him and speak with him. If he holds his ground, saying, ‘I do not want her as my wife,’

his brother’s widow will walk up to him while the elders look on, slip his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face. Her words will be: ‘So it goes for the man who refuses to rebuild his brother’s house.’
His own family will be known in Israel as ‘the house of the sandal pulled off.’

“Two men may be fighting, and the wife of one steps in to save her husband from his attacker. She reaches out and seizes the other man by his private parts. In that case you must cut off her hand. Have no pity.
Do not spare her.
“Do not carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Do not keep two different measures at home, a large one and a small one.
Use only accurate and fair weights and measures,{b} so that you live long in the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
Yahweh your God detests everyone who does these things, everyone who cheats.
“Remember how the Amalekites treated you as you left Egypt.
You were weary and exhausted when they met you on the road and struck down all the stragglers at the back. They had no fear of God.
Once Yahweh your God has given you peace from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you to own, you must erase the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!”

notes.text: Hebrew yabam, the levirate duty, from Latin levir, “husband’s brother.”
Hebrew “ephah,” a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (22 liters), standing here for measures of capacity in general. Verse 14 likewise has “an ephah and an ephah,” that is, two different measures.

verses.text: “After you enter the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, take possession of it, and make your homes there,
collect some of the first fruit of everything the soil produces in that land. Place it in a basket and carry it to the place where Yahweh your God picks to make his name live.
Go to the priest serving at that time and tell him, ‘Today I declare to Yahweh your God that I have arrived in the land Yahweh promised our ancestors with an oath, to give to us.’
The priest will accept the basket from you and put it down in front of Yahweh your God’s altar.

Then, in the presence of Yahweh your God, you will say, ‘My ancestor was an Aramean{a} who wandered, on the edge of death. He went down to Egypt, a handful of people staying as foreigners. There they grew into a great, strong, and numerous nation.
The Egyptians were cruel to us, crushed us, and put us to hard labor.
We called out to Yahweh, the God of our ancestors. Yahweh heard us and saw our suffering, our toil, and our misery.
With great power and a strong arm, with terrifying acts, signs, and wonders, Yahweh brought us out of Egypt.
He brought us here and gave us this country, rich with milk and honey.
Now, see, I am bringing the first produce of the soil that you, Yahweh, gave me.’ Place it before Yahweh your God and bow low in his presence.
Then celebrate all the good things Yahweh your God has given you and your household, you along with the Levite and the foreigner living among you.

“In the third year, the year of the tenth, you will finish setting aside a tenth of all your produce and give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so they can eat in your towns until they are full.

Then you will say in the presence of Yahweh your God, ‘I have taken the holy portion out of my house and given it to the Levite, the widow, the orphan, and the foreigner, exactly as you ordered. I have broken none of your commands, and I have forgotten none.
I did not eat any of it while grieving, take any of it out while I was unclean, or give any of it to the dead. I have obeyed Yahweh my God and done everything you ordered.
Look down from your holy home in heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land you gave us, just as you swore to our ancestors, a land rich with milk and honey.’
“Today Yahweh your God orders you to follow these laws and decisions. Keep them faithfully, with every bit of your heart and soul.
Today you have agreed that Yahweh is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his laws, commands, and decisions, and listen to him.
Today Yahweh has agreed that you are his own people, his treasure, as he promised, and that you will keep every one of his commands.
He will place you high above all the nations he has made, for fame, praise, and honor. You will belong wholly to Yahweh your God, a holy people, as he said.”

notes.text: Or “a perishing Aramean” or “an Aramean about to perish,” probably referring to Jacob. The Greek Old Testament reads “My father abandoned Syria.”

verses.text: Moses and the elders of Israel then gave the people this order: “Keep every command I lay on you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land Yahweh your God is giving you, stand up some big stones and coat them with plaster.

Once across, write every word of this teaching on them. That way you will go into the land Yahweh your God is giving you, a land rich with milk and honey, just as Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, promised.
When you have crossed the Jordan, put these stones on Mount Ebal,{a} as I order you today, and plaster them over.
Build an altar there for Yahweh your God, a stone altar, and let no iron tool be used on the stones.
Build Yahweh your God’s altar from uncut fieldstones, and burn offerings on it to Yahweh your God.
Also sacrifice fellowship offerings there, eating them and rejoicing before Yahweh your God.
On the stones, write every word of this teaching in clear, plain letters.”
Then Moses and the Levite priests spoke to all Israel: “Quiet, Israel, and listen! Today you have become the people of Yahweh your God.
So obey Yahweh your God, and follow the commands and laws I am giving you today.”
That same day Moses gave the people another order:
“After you have crossed the Jordan, six tribes will stand on Mount Gerizim{b} to pronounce the blessing: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
The other six will stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
Then the Levites will shout out to every Israelite:
‘Cursed is anyone who makes an idol, carved or cast in metal, the work of a craftsman’s hands, which Yahweh hates, and who sets it up in secret.’ All the people will answer, ‘Amen.’{c}
‘Cursed is anyone who shows contempt for his father or mother.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sends a blind person the wrong way down the road.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who denies justice to a foreigner, an orphan, or a widow.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife, since he has uncovered his father’s bed.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with an animal.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, a daughter of either his father or his mother.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his wife’s mother.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who secretly murders his neighbor.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who fails to keep the words of this teaching by doing them.’ All the people will say, ‘Amen.’”

notes.text: The Samaritan Pentateuch is reported to read “Mount Gerizim” here, and some scholars think that reading may be older; this needs further study.
Gerizim and Ebal are the two mountains on either side of Shechem.
Amen means “so be it” or “surely.”

verses.text: “Listen faithfully to Yahweh your God and carefully keep every command I give you today, and Yahweh your God will set you above all other nations on earth.
Obey Yahweh your God, and all these blessings will come to you and overtake you:
Blessed are you in the town, and blessed in the country.
Blessed are your children, your crops, and the young of your livestock, both calves and lambs.
Blessed are your basket and your kneading bowl.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed when you go out.
“Yahweh will let you defeat the enemies who attack you. They will come at you down one road and scatter from you down seven.
Yahweh will send his blessing on your barns and on all your work, and he will bless you in the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
Yahweh will establish you as a people set apart for himself, as he swore to you, provided you keep Yahweh your God’s commands and live by his ways.
All the peoples on earth will see you carry Yahweh’s name,{a} and they will be afraid of you.
Yahweh will make you overflow with good things: children, young animals, and crops, in the land Yahweh promised your ancestors with an oath that he would give you.
Yahweh will throw open the heavens, his treasury, to give your land rain at the right time and to bless everything you do. You will make loans to many nations and take none yourself.
Yahweh will make you the head and not the tail. You will rise and never fall, if you listen to the commands of Yahweh your God that I give you today, and keep them carefully,
and do not stray from any of the words I order you today, either right or left, by following other gods and serving them.
“But suppose you refuse to listen to Yahweh your God and do not carefully follow his commands and laws that I give you today. Then all these curses will come to you and overtake you:
Cursed are you in the town, and cursed in the country.
Cursed are your basket and your kneading bowl.
Cursed are your children, your crops, your calves, and your lambs.
Cursed are you when you come in, and cursed when you go out.
“In everything you try to do, Yahweh will send you curses, confusion, and failure, until you are destroyed and quickly ruined because of your evil deeds, since you abandoned me.
Yahweh will make disease stick to you until it has finished you off in the land you are about to enter and own.
Yahweh will strike you with wasting sickness, fever, swelling, scorching heat, and drought,{b} with crop blight and mildew. These will chase you until you die.
The sky above you will turn to bronze, and the ground below you to iron.
Yahweh will make your land’s rain into powder and dust. It will fall on you from the sky until you are wiped out.
“Yahweh will let your enemies beat you. You will go at them down one road and run from them down seven, and all the kingdoms on earth will be horrified by what happens to you.
Birds and wild animals will eat your dead bodies, and nobody will scare them off.
Yahweh will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and an itch that cannot be healed.
Yahweh will strike you with madness, blindness, and mental confusion.
At noon you will grope about like a blind man in the dark and get nowhere. Again and again you will be abused and robbed, and nobody will rescue you.
You will pledge to marry a woman, and another man will have her. You will build a house and never live in it. You will plant a vineyard and not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be butchered while you watch, and you will taste none of it. Your donkey will be dragged away in front of you and never come back. Your sheep will go to your enemies, and nobody will help you.
Your sons and daughters will be handed to another nation as you look on. You will strain your eyes for them all day long, and be helpless to do anything.
A nation you never knew will devour your land’s produce and everything you worked for. All your days you will be abused and beaten down.
What you see with your own eyes will drive you insane.
Yahweh will strike your knees and legs with sores that hurt and will not heal, spreading from your feet up to your head.
“Yahweh will send you and the king you appoint to a country unknown to you and your ancestors. There you will bow to other gods, carved from wood and stone.
Every nation where Yahweh drives you will look at you with horror and turn you into a proverb and a joke.
You will sow plenty of seed in the field and harvest little, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant vineyards and take care of them, yet you will drink none of the wine and gather no grapes, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees all through your territory, but you will have no oil to put on your skin, since the olives will drop off before they are ripe.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you, because they will be taken away as prisoners.
Swarms of locusts will claim all your trees and your land’s fruit.
The foreigner among you will climb higher and higher above you, while you drop lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will lend nothing to him. He will lead, and you will follow behind.
“All these curses will fall on you. They will chase and overtake you until you are wiped out, because you did not obey Yahweh your God or keep the commands and laws he gave you.
They will stand as a sign and a warning for you and your descendants forever.
You did not serve Yahweh your God joyfully and gladly when you had everything you needed.
So you will serve the enemies Yahweh sends against you, hungry, thirsty, naked, and in need of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
Yahweh will bring a nation against you from a distant land at the end of the earth, descending like an eagle, a people whose language you cannot understand,
a grim-faced nation that respects no old person and shows no pity to the young.
They will eat your livestock’s young and your land’s crops until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain, wine, or oil, no calves or lambs, until you are ruined.
They will besiege all your towns until your tall, fortified walls, which you trust, fall down across your land. They will besiege every town in the entire land Yahweh your God gave you.
During the siege, in the misery your enemy causes you, you will eat your own children, the sons and daughters Yahweh your God gave you.
The most gentle and refined man among you will look at his brother, his beloved wife, and his surviving children with greed,
and refuse to share with any of them the flesh of the children he is eating, since the siege and misery your enemy brings on all your towns will leave him nothing else.
The tenderest, most delicate woman among you, one so dainty she never tried to set her foot on the ground, will look with greed at her beloved husband, her son, and her daughter,
and at the afterbirth that comes from her and the children she bears. She will eat them in secret, as she has nothing else, during the siege and misery your enemy will cause in your towns.
“If you do not carefully keep all the words of this teaching written in this book, and fail to revere this glorious and awesome name, Yahweh your God,
Yahweh will send terrible plagues on you and your descendants, severe and long-lasting plagues, and painful, long-lasting diseases.
He will bring back every disease of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will stick to you.
Yahweh will also send you every illness and plague not recorded in this book of teaching, until you are wiped out.
You once were as many as the stars of the sky, yet only a few will be left, since you did not obey Yahweh your God.
Just as Yahweh took pleasure in making you prosper and multiply, so he will take pleasure in destroying and ruining you. You will be pulled up from the land you are about to enter and own.
“Yahweh will scatter you through every nation, from one end of the earth to the far other. There you will bow to gods of wood and stone that you and your ancestors never knew.
Among those nations you will find no peace and no place to rest your feet. Yahweh will give you a trembling heart, weak eyes, and a hopeless spirit there.
Your life will dangle in front of you. Night and day you will be terrified, never sure you will live.
In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were evening!’ and in the evening, ‘If only it were morning!’ because of the terror in your heart and the sights before your eyes.
Yahweh will ship you back to Egypt, on a road I told you that you would never see again. You will put yourselves up for sale to your enemies as slaves, men and women alike, and no one will want you.”

notes.text: Hebrew “that Yahweh’s name is called over you,” an expression of ownership.
Or “sword,” following a different vocalization of the Hebrew.

verses.text: These are the terms of the covenant that Yahweh ordered Moses to make for the Israelites during their stay in Moab, a covenant separate from the one made at Horeb.{a}
Moses called all Israel together and told them: “You watched everything Yahweh did in Egypt, against Pharaoh, all his officials, and his entire country.
You saw the great trials, the signs, and the amazing wonders.
But to this day Yahweh has not given you a mind to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
Forty years I led you across the wilderness. Your clothes never wore out on you, and the sandals on your feet never wore out.
You had no bread to eat and no wine or other strong drink, so that you would learn that I am Yahweh your God.
When you arrived here, Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, came out to fight us, and we defeated them.
We took their land and handed it over as an inheritance: Reuben’s tribe, Gad’s tribe, and half of Manasseh’s tribe received it.
Therefore keep the words of this covenant and obey them, and everything you do will succeed.
“All of you stand here today in front of Yahweh your God: your leaders, tribes, elders, and officers, all the men of Israel,
your children and wives, and the foreigners in your camp who chop your firewood and carry your water.
You are here to enter into the covenant of Yahweh your God, confirmed with an oath, which Yahweh your God is making with you today.
By it he makes you his people today, and he will be your God, as he promised you and swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your ancestors.
This covenant, with its oath, is made with more than you alone.
It also includes those standing here with us before Yahweh our God, and those who are absent today.
“You know how we lived in Egypt, and you remember how we made our way through the nations on the road here.
You saw their disgusting images, the idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold that they kept.
Make sure no man or woman, family or tribe among you turns away from Yahweh our God today to go and serve those nations’ gods. Make sure no root among you grows poisonous and bitter fruit.

Someone may hear the words of this oath and still congratulate himself, thinking, ‘I will be fine even if I follow my own stubborn heart.’ That would bring ruin on the well-watered and the dry land alike.{b}
Yahweh will never agree to forgive him. His anger and jealousy will smolder against that man, every curse written in this book will fall on him, and Yahweh will erase his name from under heaven.
Yahweh will separate him from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with all the curses of the covenant written in this book of teaching.
Future generations, your children who come after you, and foreigners from distant countries will see the plagues and diseases Yahweh has sent on that land.

The entire land will be a wasteland of sulfur and salt, with nothing planted, nothing sprouting, and no plant growing, like the destruction of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which Yahweh destroyed in his anger and fury.
All the nations will ask, ‘Why has Yahweh treated this land this way? Why such terrible, burning anger?’
People will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of Yahweh, the God of their ancestors, which was made with them when he led them out of Egypt.
They went off to serve and bow to other gods, ones they had never known and he had never assigned to them.
This is why Yahweh’s anger flared against this land, and he brought on it every curse written in this book.
In anger, fury, and great wrath, Yahweh pulled them out of their land and threw them into another country, where they remain to this day.’
“What is hidden belongs to Yahweh our God. But what he has shown belongs to us and our children always,{c} so that we may follow all the words of this teaching.”

notes.text: Verse 1 is 28:69 in the Hebrew text, and verses 2-29 are numbered 1-28.
Hebrew “to sweep away the watered with the dry,” probably a proverb meaning total destruction.
In the Hebrew text the words “to us and to our children” are marked with extraordinary dots, whose meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: “All these things, the blessing and the curse I have put in front of you, will happen to you. When you think about them in the nations where Yahweh your God has scattered you,
and you turn back to Yahweh your God and obey him in everything I order you today, you and your children, with all your heart and soul,
then Yahweh your God will restore your fortunes{a} and show you pity. From every nation where he scattered you, he will collect you again.
Even if some of you are driven to the farthest edge of the sky, Yahweh your God will round you up from there and bring you home.
Yahweh your God will lead you into the country your ancestors owned, and you will own it. He will make you prosper and grow more numerous than they were.
Yahweh your God will cut away the hardness from your heart and from your descendants’ hearts, so that you love Yahweh your God with all your heart and soul and so live.
Yahweh your God will place all these curses on the enemies who hate and persecute you.
You will obey Yahweh again and keep every one of his commands that I give you today.

Yahweh your God will fill all your work with good things, and your children, your animals’ young, and your crops will multiply. Yahweh will again take joy in your well-being, as he did in your ancestors’,
provided you obey Yahweh your God by keeping his commands and laws written in this book of teaching, and turn to Yahweh your God with all your heart and soul.
“What I command you today is not too hard for you, and it is not far away.
It is not in heaven, so you would have to ask, ‘Who will climb up to heaven, fetch it, and announce it to us so we can obey?’
It is not across the sea, so you would have to ask, ‘Who will cross the sea, get it, and tell it to us so we can obey?’
The word is very near you. It lives in your mouth and your heart, so you are able to obey it.
“Listen, today I am putting life and prosperity in front of you, along with death and disaster.

I am ordering you today to love Yahweh your God, walk in his ways, and keep his commands, laws, and decisions. Then you will live and increase, and Yahweh your God will bless you in the land you are about to enter and own.{b}
But if your heart turns away, you refuse to listen, and you are lured into bowing to other gods and serving them,
I declare to you now that you will surely be destroyed. You will not enjoy long life on the ground you are crossing the Jordan to enter and own.
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today. Set before you are life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life, so both you and your descendants may live,
by loving Yahweh your God, obeying him, and holding tight to him. He is your life and gives you long years in the land he swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your ancestors.”

notes.text: Or “bring you back from captivity.”
The Greek Old Testament begins this verse, “If you listen to the commands of the Lord your God, which I command you this day,” a clause missing from the traditional Hebrew text.

verses.text: Moses went and spoke{a} these words to all Israel.
He told them, “I am 120 years old today. My days of coming and going are over. Yahweh has also told me, ‘This Jordan is one you will not cross.’
Yahweh your God himself will cross ahead of you. He will wipe out these nations before you so that you take their place. As Yahweh has said, Joshua will be the one to lead you across.
Yahweh will treat them as he treated the Amorite kings Sihon and Og and their land, which he wiped out.
Yahweh will give them to you, and you must deal with them in exactly the way I have ordered.
Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, because Yahweh your God goes with you. He will never leave you or abandon you.”

Moses then called Joshua and told him in front of all Israel, “Be strong and brave, since you will go with this people into the land Yahweh swore to their ancestors he would give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance.
Yahweh himself goes ahead of you and will be with you. He will never leave you or abandon you. Have no fear and do not lose heart.”
Moses wrote down this teaching and gave it to the Levite priests who carried the chest of Yahweh’s covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses ordered them, “At the end of every seventh year, the set time for canceling debts, during the Feast of Booths,{b}
when all Israel comes before Yahweh your God at the place he picks, read this teaching aloud to all Israel.
Gather the people, men, women, children, and the foreigners in your towns, so that they can hear, learn to revere Yahweh your God, and carefully follow every word of this teaching.
Their children, who have never heard it, will hear it and learn to revere Yahweh your God for the whole time you live in the country across the Jordan that you are about to own.”

Yahweh told Moses, “Your death is near. Call Joshua, and the two of you present yourselves at the meeting tent, where I will commission him.” Moses and Joshua went and took up positions at the meeting tent.
Yahweh appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar stood at the tent’s entrance.

Yahweh told Moses, “You will soon die and join your ancestors. Then these people will rise up and chase after the foreign gods of the land they are entering, like an unfaithful wife. They will turn from me and break the covenant I made with their nation.

On that day my anger will flare up against them. I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured. Many disasters and troubles will strike them, and on that day they will ask, ‘Have these disasters come on us because our God is not with us?’
On that day I will certainly hide my face from them, for all the wrong they will have committed by turning to other gods.
“Now compose this song for yourselves and teach it to the Israelites. Have them learn it by heart, so the song can stand as my witness against them.

The land I swore to their ancestors is rich with milk and honey, and I will take them into it. They will eat their fill and grow fat, and then they will chase after other gods and worship them. Me they will reject, and my covenant they will break.

When many disasters and troubles overtake them, this song will speak against them, since their descendants will never forget it. I know what they are planning even now, before I have led them into the land I swore to give them.”
Moses wrote this song down that day and taught it to the Israelites.
Yahweh{c} commissioned Joshua son of Nun, saying, “Be strong and brave. You are the one who will bring the Israelites into the country I promised them by oath, and I myself will stay by your side.”
Moses wrote every word of this teaching in a book, right to its end.
he gave this order to the Levites, the carriers of the chest of Yahweh’s covenant:
“Take this book of teaching and place it beside the chest of the covenant of Yahweh your God, where it will remain as a witness against you.
You are stubborn and rebellious, and I know it. If you have rebelled against Yahweh even now, while I am alive among you, how much more after I die!
Gather your tribal elders and officials to me. I will speak these words in their hearing, and I will call heaven and earth to testify against them.

After my death, I know, you will become completely corrupt and leave the way I ordered you to follow. In later days disaster will come on you, because you will do what is evil in Yahweh’s sight and make him angry by what your hands have made.”
Then Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end, while the whole assembly of Israel listened:

notes.text: The Greek Old Testament reads “Moses finished speaking,” and a Qumran manuscript is reported to agree; the difference involves two similar Hebrew words.
Held in the seventh month, Tishri (September-October).
Hebrew “he”; the context shows that Yahweh is meant. The Greek Old Testament makes Moses the subject.

verses.text:
“Listen, skies above, for I have words to speak!
Earth below, hear what my mouth declares.

May my teaching drop down like rain,
and my speech settle like morning dew,
like soft drizzle on young grass,
like pouring storms on garden plants.

I will call out the name of Yahweh.
Come, declare how great our God is!

“He is the Rock, and everything he makes is flawless.
All his ways are fair.
Faithful and never crooked,
he is honest and straight in all he does.

Yet they have wronged him. Because of their stain,{a} they are no longer his children.
They are a twisted, warped generation.

Is this how you thank Yahweh,
you senseless and foolish people?
Is he not your father, the one who bought you,{b}
who shaped you and set you on your feet?

“Think back to ancient days.
Reflect on the years of earlier generations.
Ask your father and he will explain it,
ask your elders and they will tell you.

But Yahweh’s own share was his people,
and Jacob was the land measured out for him.

“He came upon Jacob in a desert country,
in a barren, howling wasteland.
He circled around him and cared for him,
and kept him safe as the pupil{f} of his own eye.

Like an eagle stirring up its nest
and fluttering above its chicks,
he spread his wings and caught Israel,
and carried him on his feathers.

Yahweh alone led him.
No foreign god stood at his side.

He set him on the high places of the land,
so Israel lived on what the fields produced.
He gave him honey from a cliff to suck
and oil from hard rock.

There was cream from the cattle and milk from the sheep,
the fat of lambs and of rams bred in Bashan,
and of goats, along with the finest wheat grain.
Your drink was wine pressed from grapes, bubbling red like blood.

“Then Jeshurun{g} got fat and lashed out.
You got fat, thick, and stuffed.
He turned his back on the God who had made him
and looked down on the Rock who saved him.

They stirred up his jealousy with foreign gods
and enraged him with disgusting practices.

They offered sacrifices to demons, who are not God,
to gods unknown to them before,
to newcomers who had just appeared,
gods your ancestors had never feared.

You overlooked the Rock who fathered you
and lost sight of the God who gave you birth.

“Yahweh watched this happen and rejected them,
angered by his sons and daughters.

‘I will turn my face away from them,’ he said.
‘Let me see how it all ends for them.
They are a crooked generation,
children who cannot be trusted.

“‘They made me jealous by worshiping what is no god
and enraged me with their useless idols.{h}
So I will make them jealous with a people who are not a people,
and anger them with a foolish nation.

A fire has been lit by my anger,
and it burns all the way down to the deepest part of Sheol.{i}
It eats up the earth and what grows on it
and sets the foundations of the mountains aflame.

“‘I will pile calamities on them
and shoot every arrow I have into them.

They will waste away from famine,
and be eaten up by fever and bitter plague.
I will send animals with fangs against them,
together with snakes that slither in the dust and carry poison.

In the streets the sword will leave families childless,
and indoors there will be terror.
Young men and young women will die,
and so will nursing babies and white-haired elders.

I said I would scatter them{j}
and wipe out any memory of them from among humanity.

But I worried that the enemy would sneer,
that their foes would misread what happened.
They might say, “We won by our own power.
Yahweh had nothing to do with it.”’

“Israel is a nation with no sense,
and not one of them has any understanding.

If they were wise, they would work this out
and think about how it will end for them.

How could one soldier chase a thousand,
or two put ten thousand to flight,
unless their Rock had sold them off,
unless Yahweh had handed them over?

Their rock is nothing like our Rock.
Even our enemies can see that.

Their vine springs from Sodom’s vine,
from the terraces of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are poisonous,
and their bunches are bitter.

Their wine is the venom of snakes,
the deadly poison of cobras.

“‘Have I not kept this stored up,
locked away in my vaults?

Revenge and payment belong to me,{k}
for the time when their feet slip.
Their day of ruin is close,
and their doom is hurrying toward them.’

Yahweh will defend his people,
and take pity on his servants,
once he sees that their strength is gone,
and that slave and free alike have vanished.

Then he will ask, ‘Where are their gods now,
the rock they ran to for protection,

who ate the fat of their sacrifices
and drank the wine of their drink offerings?
Let them stand up and help you.
Let them be your shelter!

“‘Understand that I alone am he.
No god exists beside me.
I kill, and I bring to life.
I injure, and I also heal,
and no one can pull anyone out of my grasp.

I lift my hand toward heaven and swear
by my own endless life:

When I sharpen my flashing sword
and take hold of justice with my hand,
my enemies will get their revenge from me,
and those who hate me will be paid back.
Moses came with Hoshea{o} son of Nun and spoke every word of this song aloud, so that all the people could hear it.
When Moses had finished reciting all of this to the whole nation,
he told them, “Take to heart every word I am warning you with today. Then you can order your children to be careful to follow every word of this teaching.
These words are not trivial. They are your life! Through them you will live long on the ground you are crossing the Jordan to take.”
That same day Yahweh spoke to Moses:
“Go up into the Abarim range,{p} to Mount Nebo in Moab, which faces Jericho. Look out over Canaan, the country I am giving to the Israelites as their own.
On the mountain you climb, you will die and be gathered to your relatives, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his.
You both broke trust with me among the Israelites at Meribah-kadesh’s waters{q} in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not honor me as holy in their presence.
You may look at the land from far off, but you may not enter the country I am giving to the Israelites.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of this line is obscure. The Greek Old Testament reads “spotted children.”
Or “created you.”
Hebrew Elyon, a title of God meaning “highest.”
Or “humankind”; Hebrew “the sons of Adam.”

This follows the traditional Hebrew text. A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran reads “the sons of God,” and many scholars think that is the earlier reading. The Greek Old Testament reads “the angels of God.” The difference bears on whether the nations were assigned to heavenly beings under the Most High (compare 4:19; 29:26). This needs scholarly review.
Hebrew “the little man of his eye.”
Jeshurun means “upright one,” a poetic name for Israel. The Greek Old Testament reads “So Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked.”
Hebrew hebel, “vapor” or “breath.”
Sheol is the realm of the dead.
The Hebrew is uncertain; perhaps “cut them in pieces” or “blow them away.”
The Greek Old Testament reads “In the day of vengeance I will repay.” Romans 12:19 and Hebrews 10:30 quote this line as “Vengeance is mine; I will repay.”
Or “from the heads of the enemy’s leaders.”
Or “Praise his people, you nations.” The traditional Hebrew wording is brief and can be read several ways.

This verse is much longer in other ancient witnesses. The Greek Old Testament has the heavens rejoicing with him, the angels of God worshiping him, the nations celebrating with his people, and the sons of God taking strength in him. It then says he will avenge the blood of his sons, repay his enemies, reward those who hate him, and cleanse the land of his people. A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran is also reported to have a longer text.

Hoshea means “salvation,” the earlier name of Joshua (Numbers 13:16). The Greek Old Testament reads “Joshua,” and it also begins this verse, “And Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.”
Abarim means “regions beyond,” the range east of the Jordan facing Jericho.
Meribah means “quarreling”; see Numbers 20:1-13.

subheads.44: Moses Told to Climb Mount Nebo

verses.text: This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, pronounced over the Israelites shortly before his death.

He said:
“Yahweh came from Sinai.
He dawned over them from Seir,
and blazed out from Mount Paran.
Among tens of thousands of holy ones he arrived,{a}
with fiery flames{b} at his right hand.

He truly cherishes the peoples.{c}
Every one of his holy ones is held in your hand.
They sit down at your feet
and take in your words.

Moses handed us a teaching,
a treasure for Jacob’s assembly.

Yahweh became king over Jeshurun
when the people’s leaders gathered,
and all the tribes of Israel stood together.

“Let Reuben stay alive and not die out,
even if his men are few.”

About Judah he said:
“Listen, Yahweh, to Judah’s cry,
and bring him back to his own people.
His hands fight to defend him,{d}
so help him against his enemies.”

About Levi he said:
“Your Thummim and Urim{e} belong to the man loyal to you,
the one you tested at Massah
and quarreled with at the waters of Meribah.

Of his own father and mother he said, ‘I have never seen them.’
He would not recognize his brothers
or even claim his sons and daughters.
Yet your word they have kept,
and they have guarded your covenant.

They teach Jacob your rulings
and Israel your teaching.
They offer incense in your presence{f}
and complete burnt offerings on your altar.

Yahweh, bless his strength
and accept the work of his hands.
Crush the hips of those who rise against him,
and of his haters, so they never stand again.”

About Benjamin he said:
“Yahweh’s beloved lives secure beside him.
All day long Yahweh covers him,
and he rests between Yahweh’s shoulders.”{g}

About Joseph he said:
“May Yahweh bless his land
with the best that heaven offers, with dew,
and with water from the deep that lies below,

with the best that ripens in the sun
and the finest crops each month brings in,{h}

with the choicest from the age-old mountains
and the bounty of the everlasting hills,

with the best the earth and all it holds can give,
and the goodwill of the one who dwelt in the bush.
May all this rest on Joseph’s head,
on the forehead of the one set apart from his brothers.

He is like a firstborn bull in splendor,
and his horns are like a wild ox’s horns.
With them he will gore the nations,
to the far ends of the earth.
Those horns are Ephraim’s ten thousands,
and Manasseh’s thousands.”

About Zebulun he said:
“Zebulun, be glad when you head out,
and Issachar, be glad in your tents.

They invite the nations up to the mountain,
and there they offer sacrifices that are right.
They feed on the riches of the seas
and on treasure buried in the sand.”

About Gad he said:
“Blessed is the one who gives Gad room to spread!
Gad crouches like a lioness,
ready to rip off an arm, even a head.

He picked out the best land for himself,
since a commander’s share was saved for him there.
He came with the leaders of the people,
and he carried out Yahweh’s justice
and his rulings for Israel.”

About Dan he said:
“Dan is a lion cub
leaping out of Bashan.”

About Naphtali he said:
“Naphtali, you are full of favor
and loaded with Yahweh’s blessing.
Take as yours the lake{i} and the south.”

About Asher he said:
“Of all the sons, Asher has the greatest blessing.
May his brothers be pleased with him,
and may olive oil bathe his feet.

May the bars on your gates be iron and bronze,
and may your strength{j} last as long as you live.

“No one compares to God, Jeshurun.
He crosses the sky to come to your aid,
and rides the clouds in his glory.

The ancient God is where you live,{k}
and under you are his everlasting arms.
He pushed the enemy out ahead of you
and ordered, ‘Wipe them out!’

So Israel lives in safety,
and Jacob’s spring flows undisturbed,{l}
in a land of grain and new wine,
where the skies drip dew.

You are fortunate, Israel! Who else is like you,
a people rescued by Yahweh?
He is your shield and your helper,
the sword that wins your victory.
Your enemies will shrink back from you,
and you will walk over their high places.”{m}

notes.text: Or “from Ribeboth-kodesh,” perhaps a place name. The Greek Old Testament reads “with the ten thousands of Kadesh.”
The Hebrew is uncertain. The written Hebrew has one obscure word, which is traditionally read as two words, “fire of law.” The Greek Old Testament reads “on his right hand were his angels with him.”
Or “his people.” The Greek Old Testament reads “he spared his people.”
Or “his hands are enough for him.”

The Urim and Thummim were the priestly lots used to seek God’s will; the names may mean “lights” and “perfections.” The Greek Old Testament begins, “Give to Levi,” and a Qumran manuscript is reported to read similarly.
Hebrew “in your nostrils.”
Or “and he lives among his slopes,” perhaps a reference to the temple hill in Benjamin’s territory.
Or “moons.”
Or “the west.” Hebrew yam can mean “sea” or “west”; here it is perhaps the Sea of Galilee.
The Hebrew is uncertain; the word may mean “strength” or “rest.”
Or “refuge.”
Or “alone.”
Or “trample on their backs.”

verses.text: Moses climbed from the plains of Moab up Mount Nebo, to the peak of Pisgah opposite Jericho. Yahweh let him see the entire land: Gilead all the way to Dan,
the whole territory of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all of Judah as far as the western sea,{a}
the Negev,{b} and the plain around Jericho, the city of palms, reaching to Zoar.

Yahweh told him, “This is the country I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, when I swore, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it.”
Moses, Yahweh’s servant, died there in Moab, just as Yahweh had said it would happen.{c}
Yahweh buried him{d} in a valley in Moab, across from Beth Peor, but the location of the grave has stayed a mystery up to the present.
At his death Moses was 120. His eyes were still sharp, and his strength had not faded.
The Israelites wept for thirty days over Moses on the plains of Moab, until the period of crying and mourning for him ended.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. The Israelites therefore listened to Joshua and did as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
No prophet in Israel has risen since to equal Moses, the one Yahweh knew face to face.
No one else matches the signs and wonders that Yahweh sent him to perform in Egypt, against Pharaoh, all his officials, and his whole country,
or the mighty power and the great and fearsome deeds Moses displayed before all Israel.

notes.text: That is, the Mediterranean.
Negev means “dry land,” the arid south of Judah.
Hebrew “at the mouth of Yahweh.” Later Jewish tradition read this as “by the kiss of Yahweh.”
That is, Yahweh buried him. Or “he was buried.” The Greek Old Testament reads “they buried him.”
